regex: 106020: Deny IP teardrop fragment \(size = (?<size>\d+), offset = (?<offset>\d+)\) from (?<src_ip>[0-9.]+) to (?<dest_ip>[0-9.]+)
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA discarded an IP packet with a teardrop signature containing either a small offset or fragment overlapping. This is a hostile event that circumvents the Secure Firewall ASA or an Intrusion Detection System.

regex: 106023:\s*(?<action>\S+)\s+(?<transport>\S+)(?:\s+(?<protocol_id>\d+))?\s+src\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<src_ip>\S+)\s+dst\s+(?<dest_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<dest_ip>\S+)(?:\s*\(type\s+(?<icmp_type>\d+),\s+code\s+(?<icmp_code>\d+)\))?\s+by\s+access-group\s+"(?<access_group>[^"]+)"\s+\[(?<hash_codes>[^\]]+)\]
explanation: A real IP packet was denied by the ACL. This message appears even if you do not have the log option enabled for an ACL. The IP address is the real IP address instead of the values that display through NAT. Both user identity information and FQDN information is provided for the IP addresses if a matched one is found. The Secure Firewall ASA logs either identity information (domain\user) or FQDN (if the username is not available). If the identity information or FQDN is available, the Secure Firewall ASA logs this information for both the source and destination.

regex: 106027:\s*(?<action>\S+)\s+(?<transport>\S+)\s+src\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<src_mac>\S+)\s+dst\s+(?<dest_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<dest_mac>\S+)\s+by\s+access-group\s+"(?<access_group>[^"]+)"
explanation: An non IP packet was denied by the ACL. This message is displayed even if you do not have the log option enabled for an extended ACL.

The initial occurrence or the total number of occurrences during an interval are listed. This message provides more information than message 106023, which only logs denied packets, and does not include the hit count or a configurable level. When an access-list line has the log argument, it is expected that this message ID might be triggered because of a nonsynchronized packet reaching the Secure Firewall ASA and being evaluated by the access list. For example, if an ACK packet is received on the Secure Firewall ASA (for which no TCP connection exists in the connection table), the Secure Firewall ASA might generate message 106100, indicating that the packet was permitted; however, the packet is later correctly dropped because of no matching connection. The following list describes the message values:
A packet was either permitted or denied by an access-list that was applied through a VPN filter. This message is the VPN/AAA filter equivalent of message 106100.
A packet was denied by an access-list that was applied through a VPN filter. This message is the VPN/AAA filter equivalent of message106023.

The Secure Firewall ASA received a RIP reply message with bad authentication. This message might be caused by a misconfiguration on the router or the Secure Firewall ASA or by an unsuccessful attempt to attack the routing table of the Secure Firewall ASA.
This event is generated when an ESMTP message size exceeds the size declared in the RCPT command.

regex: 109011: Authen Session Start: (?<user_2>\S+) '(?<user>\S+)', sid (?<number>\S+)$
explanation: An authentication session started between the host and the Secure Firewall ASA and has not yet completed.

regex: 109012: Authen Session End: (?<user_2>\S+) '(?<user>\S+)', sid (?<number>\S+), elapsed (?<number_2>\S+) seconds$
explanation: The authentication cache has timed out. Users must reauthenticate on their next connection. You can change the duration of this timer with the timeout uauth command.

The response from the AAA server cannot be validated. The configured server key is probably incorrect. This message may be displayed during transactions with RADIUS or TACACS+ servers. The server_IP_address is the IP address of the relevant AAA server. The user is the user name associated with the connection.

regex: 109032: Unable to install ACL '(?<access_list>\S+)', downloaded for (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+); Error in ACE: '(?<ace>\S+)'$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received an access control list from a RADIUS server to apply to a user connection, but an entry in the list contains a syntax error. Th euse of a list containing an error could result in the violation of a security policy, so the Secure Firewall ASA failed to authenticate the user.

regex: 109038: Attribute (?<internal_attribute_name>\S+) value "(?<string_from_server>.+?)" from AAA server could not be parsed as a (?<type>\S+)$
explanation: The AAA subsystem tried to parse an attribute from the AAA server into an internal representation and failed.

regex: 109100: Received (?<coa>\S+) update from (?<coa_source_ip>\S+) for (?<user_2>\S+) "(?<user>\S+)", with session ID (?<audit_session_id>\S+), changing authorization attributes\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has successfully processed the CoA policy update request from coa-source-ip for user username with session id audit-session-id . This syslog message is generated after a change of authorization policy update has been received by the Secure Firewall ASA, validated and applied. In a non-error case, this is the only syslog message that is generated when a change of authorization is received and processed.

regex: 109101: Received (?<coa>\S+) disconnect request from (?<coa_source_ip>\S+) for (?<user_2>\S+) "(?<user>\S+)", with session ID: (?<audit_session_id>\S+)\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received a correctly formatted Disconnect-Request for an active VPN session and has successfully terminated the connection.

explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received a valid change of authorization request, but the session ID specified in the request does not match any active sessions on the Secure Firewall ASA. This could be the result of the change of authorization server attempting to issue a change of authorization on a session that has already been closed by the user.

regex: 109103: (?<coa>\S+) (?<action_type>\S+) from (?<coa_source_ip>\S+) failed for (?<user_2>\S+) "(?<user>\S+)", with session ID: (?<audit_session_id>\S+)\.$

regex: 313001: (?<action>\w+) (?<transport>\w+) type=(?<icmp_type>\d+), code=(?<icmp_code>\S+) from (?<src_ip>[0-9.]+) on interface (?<src_interface>\S+)
explanation: When using the icmp command with an access list, if the first matched entry is a permit entry, the ICMP packet continues processing. If the first matched entry is a deny entry, or an entry is not matched, the Secure Firewall ASA discards the ICMP packet and generates this message. The icmp command enables or disables pinging to an interface. With pinging disabled, the Secure Firewall ASA cannot be detected on the network. This feature is also referred to as configurable proxy pinging.

regex: 313004:\s*(?<action>\S+)\s+(?<transport>\S+)\s+type=(?<icmp_type>\d+),\s+from\s+laddr\s+(?<src_ip>\S+)\s+on\s+interface\s+(?<src_interface>.+?)\s+to\s+(?<dest_ip>\S+):\s+(?<reason>.+)
explanation: ICMP packets were dropped by the Secure Firewall ASA because of security checks added by the stateful ICMP feature that are usually either ICMP echo replies without a valid echo request already passed across the Secure Firewall ASA or ICMP error messages not related to any TCP, UDP, or ICMP session already established in the Secure Firewall ASA.

regex: 313005:\s*No\s+matching\s+connection\s+for\s+(?<transport>\S+)\s+error\s+message:\s+icmp\s+src\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<src_ip>\S+)\s+dst\s+(?<dest_interface>[^:\s]+):(?<dest_ip>[^\(\s]+)(?:\((?<dest_host>[^\)]+)\))?\s+\(type\s+(?<icmp_type>\d+),\s*code\s+(?<icmp_code>\d+)\)\s+on\s+(?<interface_name>\S+)\s+interface\.\s+Original\s+IP\s+payload:\s+(?:(?<orig_transport>\S+)\s+src\s+(?<orig_src_ip>\S+)(?:\/(?<src_port>\d+))?\s+dst\s+(?<orig_dest_ip>\S+)(?:\/(?<dest_port>\d+))?(?:\s+\(type\s+(?<orig_icmp_type>\d+),\s*code\s+(?<orig_icmp_code>\d+)\))?|(?<orig_msg>.*))\.
explanation: ICMP error packets were dropped by the Secure Firewall ASA because the ICMP error messages are not related to any session already established in the Secure Firewall ASA.

regex: 313008: (?<action>\w+) (?<transport>\S+) type=(?<icmp_type>\d+), code=(?<icmp_code>\S+) from (?<src_ip>\S+) on interface (?<src_interface>\S+)
explanation: When using the icmp command with an access list, if the first matched entry is a permit entry, the ICMPv6 packet continues processing. If the first matched entry is a deny entry, or an entry is not matched, the Secure Firewall ASA discards the ICMPv6 packet and generates this message. The icmp command enables or disables pinging to an interface. When pinging is disabled, the Secure Firewall ASA is undetectable on the network. This feature is also referred to as “configurable proxy pinging.”

regex: 322002: ARP inspection check failed for arp (?:request|response) received from host (?<mac_address>\S+) on (?<interface_2>\S+) (?<interface>\S+)\. This host is advertising MAC Address (?<mac_address_1>\S+) for IP Address (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), which is (?:statically|dynamically) bound to MAC Address (?<mac_address_2>\S+)$
explanation: If the ARP inspection module is enabled, it checks whether a new ARP entry advertised in the packet conforms to the statically configured or dynamically learned IP-MAC address binding before forwarding ARP packets across the Secure Firewall ASA. If this check fails, the ARP inspection module drops the ARP packet and generates this message. This situation may be caused by either ARP spoofing attacks in the network or an invalid configuration (IP-MAC binding).

regex: 323006: Module (?<ips>\S+) experienced a data channel communication failure, data channel is DOWN\.$

This failure triggers a failover when the failure occurs on the active Secure Firewall ASA in an HA configuration. The failure also results in the configured fail open or fail closed policy being enforced on traffic that would normally be sent to the services module. This message is generated whenever a communication problem over the Secure Firewall ASA dataplane occurs between the system module and the services module, which can be caused when the services module stops, resets, is removed or disabled.

explanation: Umbrella fail-open has been configured and a resolver unreachabilty has been detected.

regex: 339008: Umbrella resolver (?<current_resolver_ipv46>\S+) is unreachable, moving to fail\-close$
explanation: Umbrella fail-open has NOT been configured and a resolver unreachabilty has been detected.

regex: 342002: REST API Agent failed, reason: (?<reason>\S+)\.$
explanation: The REST API Agent could fail to start or crash for various reasons, and the reason is specified.

regex: 342006: Failed to install REST API image, reason: (?<reason>\S+)\.$
explanation: The REST API image installation may fail, for one of the following reasons: version check failed, image verification failed, image file not found, out of space on flash or mount failed.

regex: 342008: Failed to uninstall REST API image, reason: (?<reason>\S+)\.$
explanation: The REST API image could not be uninstalled for the following reasons- unmount failed or REST Agent is enabled.

regex: 402114: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<remote_ip>\S+) to (?<local_ip>\S+) with an invalid SPI\.$
explanation: An IPsec packet was received that specifies an SPI that does not exist in the SA database. This may be a temporary condition caused by slight differences in aging of SAs between the IPsec peers, or it may be because the local SAs have been cleared. It may also indicate incorrect packets sent by the IPsec peer, which may be part of an attack. This message is rate limited to no more than one message every five seconds.

regex: 402116: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<remote_ip>\S+) \(user= (?<user>\S+)\) to (?<local_ip>\S+)\. The decapsulated inner packet doesn't match the negotiated policy in the SA\. The packet specifies its destination as (?<pkt_daddr>\S+), its source as (?<pkt_saddr>\S+), and its protocol as (?<pkt_prot>\S+)\. The SA specifies its local proxy as (?<id_daddr>\S+)/(?<id_dmask>\S+)/(?<id_dprot>\S+)/(?<id_dport>\S+) and its (?<remote_proxy>\S+) as (?<id_saddr>\S+)/(?<id_smask>\S+)/(?<id_sprot>\S+)/(?<id_sport>\S+)\.$
explanation: : A decapsulated IPsec packet does not match the negotiated identity. The peer is sending other traffic through this security association, which may be caused by a security association selection error by the peer, or it may be part of an attack. This message is rate limited to no more than one message every five seconds.

regex: 402118: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<remote_ip>\S+) \(user= (?<user>\S+)\) to (?<local_ip>\S+) containing an illegal IP fragment of length (?<frag_len>\S+) with offset (?<frag_offset>\S+)\.$
explanation: A decapsulatd IPsec packet included an IP fragment with an offset less than or equal to 128 bytes. The latest version of the security architecture for IP RFC recommends 128 bytes as the minimum IP fragment offset to prevent reassembly attacks. This may be part of an attack. This message is rate limited to no more than one message every five seconds.

regex: 402119: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<remote_ip>\S+) \(user= (?<user>\S+)\) to (?<local_ip>\S+) that failed anti\-replay checking\.$
explanation: An IPsec packet was received with an invalid sequence number. The peer is sending packets including sequence numbers that may have been previously used. This message indicates that an IPsec packet has been received with a sequence number outside of the acceptable window. This packet will be dropped by IPsec as part of a possible attack. This message is rate limited to no more than one message every five seconds.

regex: 402120: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<remote_ip>\S+) \(user= (?<user>\S+)\) to (?<local_ip>\S+) that failed authentication\.$
explanation: An IPsec packet was received and failed authentication. The packet is dropped. The packet may have been corrupted in transit, or the peer may be sending invalid IPsec packets, which may indicate an attack if many of these packets were received from the same peer. This message is rate limited to no more than one message every five seconds.

regex: 402121: IPSEC: Received an (?<protocol>\S+) packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+), sequence number= (?<seq_num>\S+)\) from (?<peer_addr>\S+) \(user= (?<user>\S+)\) to (?<lcl_addr>\S+) that was dropped by IPSec \((?<drop_reason>\S+)\)\.$
explanation: An IPsec packet to be decapsulated was received and subsequently dropped by the IPsec subsystem. This may indicate a problem with the Secure Firewall ASA configuration or with the Secure Firewall ASA itself.

regex: 402123: CRYPTO: The (?<accel_type>\S+) hardware accelerator encountered an error \((?<eror_type>\S+), code= (?<error_string>.+?)\) while executing the command (?<command_name>\S+) \((?<command>\S+)\)\.$
explanation: An error was detected while running a crypto command with a hardware accelerator, which may indicate a problem with the accelerator. This type of error may occur for a variety of reasons, and this message supplements the crypto accelerator counters to help determine the cause.

regex: ^(?:%ASA-\d+-402124: CRYPTO: The (?<platform>\S+) hardware accelerator encountered an error \(HWErrAddr= 0x(?<error_address>\S+), Core= (?<error_core>\S+), (?<hwerrcode>\S+)= (?<error_code>\S+), (?<istatreg>\S+)= 0x(?<istat>\S+), (?<pcierrreg>\S+)= 0x(?<pci>\S+), (?<coreerrstat>\S+)= 0x(?<core_error_stat>\S+), (?<coreerraddr>\S+)= 0x(?<core_err_address>\S+), Doorbell Size\[0\]= (?<size>\S+), (?<doorbell>\S+) Outstanding\[0\]= (?<outstanding>\S+), Doorbell Size\[1\]= (?<size_2>\S+), (?<doorbell_2>\S+) Outstanding\[1\]= (?<outstanding_2>\S+), SWReset= (?<reset_code>\S+)\)|%ASA-\d+-402124: CRYPTO: The (?<platform>\S+) hardware accelerator encountered an error \(HWErrAddr= 0x(?<error_address>\S+), Core= (?<error_core>\S+), (?<hwerrcode>\S+)= (?<error_code>\S+), Queue= (?<queue_string>\S+) \((?<g_0>\S+)\), (?<istatreg>\S+)= 0x(?<istat>\S+), Station= (?<core_station>\S+), (?<corerptr>\S+)= 0x(?<core_pointer>\S+), (?<coreconfig>\S+)= 0x(?<core_config_pointer>\S+), SWReset= (?<reset_code>\S+)\))$
explanation: The crypto hardware chip has reported a fatal error, indicating that the chip is inoperable. The information from this message captures the details to allow further analysis of the problem. The crypto chip is reset when this condition is detected to unobtrusively allow the Secure Firewall ASA to continue functioning. Also, the crypto environment at the time this issue is detected is written to a crypto archive directory on flash to provide further debugging information. Various parameters related to the crypto hardware are included in this message, as follows:

regex: 402125: CRYPTO: The (?<platform>\S+) hardware accelerator (?<ring_string>\S+) ring timed out \(Desc= 0x(?<descriptor_address>\S+), (?<ctrlstat>\S+)= 0x(?<italic_text>.+), (?<resultp>\S+)= 0x(?<success_pointer>\S+), (?<resultval>\S+)= (?<success_value>\S+), Cmd= 0x(?<crypto_command>\S+), (?<cmdsize>\S+)= (?<command_size>\S+), Param= 0x(?<command_parameters>\S+), Dlen= (?<data_length>\S+), (?<datap>\S+)= 0x(?<data_pointer>\S+), (?<ctxtp>\S+)= 0x(?<vpn_context_pointer>\S+), SWReset= (?<reset_number>\S+)\)$
explanation: The crypto driver has detected that either the IPSEC descriptor ring or SSL/Admin descriptor ring is no longer progressing, meaning the crypto chip no longer appears to be functioning. The crypto chip is reset when this condition is detected to unobtrusively allow the Secure Firewall ASA to continue functioning. Also, the crypto environment at the time this issue was detected was written to a crypto archive directory on flash to provide further debugging information.

regex: 402128: CRYPTO: An attempt to allocate a large memory block failed, size: (?<size>\S+), limit: (?<limit>\S+)\.$
explanation: An SSL connection is attempting to use more memory than allowed. The request has been denied.

regex: 402129: CRYPTO: An attempt to release a DMA memory block failed, location: (?<address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 402130: CRYPTO: Received an ESP packet \(SPI = xxxxxxxxxx, sequence number=xxxx\) from 172\.16\.0\.1 \(user=(?<user>\S+)\) to 192\.168\.0\.2 with incorrect IPsec padding\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA crypto hardware accelerator detected an IPsec packet with invalid padding. The ATT VPN client sometimes pads IPsec packets incorrectly.

regex: 402141: CRYPTO: Key zeroization error: key set '(?<type>\S+)', reason '(?<reason>\S+)'$
explanation: An error occurred during an RSA public key pair generation.

regex: 402142: CRYPTO: Bulk data (?<op>\S+) error: algorithm '(?<alg>\S+)', mode '(?<mode>\S+)'$
explanation: An error occurred during a symmetric key operation.

regex: 402144: CRYPTO: Digital signature error: signature algorithm '(?<sig>\S+)', hash algorithm '(?<hash>\S+)'$
explanation: An error occurred during digital signature generation.

regex: 402146: CRYPTO: Keyed hash generation error: algorithm '(?<hash>\S+)', key len (?<len>\S+)$
explanation: A keyed hash generation error occurred.

regex: 403101: PPTP session state not established, but received an XGRE packet, (?<tunnel_id>\S+)=(?<number>\S+), (?<session_id>\S+)=(?<number_2>\S+)$
explanation: The ASA received a PPTP XGRE packet without a corresponding control connection session.

regex: 403102: PPP virtual (?<interface>\S+) (?<interface_name>\S+) rcvd pkt with invalid protocol: (?<protocol>\S+), reason: (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: The module received an XGRE encapsulated PPP packet with an invalid protocol field.
The module received a spoofed PPTP packet, which may indicate a hostile event.

regex: 403110: PPP virtual (?<interface>\S+) (?<interface_name>\S+), (?<user_2>\S+): (?<user>\S+) missing MPPE key from aaa server$
explanation: The AAA server was not returning the MPPE key attributes required to set up the MPPE encryption policy.
A client IP address in the network is the same as the Secure Firewall ASA interface IP address.
The module failed to allocate RAM system memory while starting a connection or has no more address translation slots available.
The Secure Firewall ASA failed to allocate RAM system memory while starting a connection or has no more address translation slots available.
The host limit was exceeded. An inside host is counted toward the limit when one of the following conditions is true:

regex: 411001: Line protocol on Interface (?<interface_name>\S+), changed state to up$
explanation: The status of the line protocol has changed from down to up . If interface_name is a logical interface name such as inside and outside, this message indicates that the logical interface line protocol has changed from down to up . If interface_name is a physical interface name such as Ethernet0 and GigabitEthernet0/1, this message indicates that the physical interface line protocol has changed from down to up .

regex: 411002: Line protocol on Interface (?<interface_name>\S+), changed state to down$
explanation: The status of the line protocol has changed from up to down. If interface_name is a logical interface name such as inside and outside, this message indicates that the logical interface line protocol has changed from up to down. In this case, the physical interface line protocol status is not affected. If interface_name is a physical interface name such as Ethernet0 and GigabitEthernet0/1, this message indicates that the physical interface line protocol has changed from up to down.

regex: 411003: Interface (?<interface_name>\S+), changed state to administratively up$
explanation: The configuration status of the interface has changed from down to up.

regex: 411004: Interface (?<interface_name>\S+), changed state to administratively down$
explanation: The configuration status of the interface has changed from down to up.

regex: 413004: Module in slot (?<string_one>\S+) failed to write software v(?<newver>\S+) \(currently v(?<ver>\S+)\), (?<reason>\S+)\. Trying again\.$
explanation: The module failed to accept a software version, and will be transitioned to an UNRESPONSIVE state. Another attempt will be made to update the module software.

regex: ^(?:%ASA-\d+-413005: Module (?<module_id>\S+), (?<application>\S+) is not supported "(?<app_name>\S+)" version "(?<app_vers>\S+)" type (?<app_type>\S+)\.|%ASA-\d+-413005: Module (?<prod_id>\S+) in slot(?<slot_num>\S+) , (?<application>\S+) is not supported (?<app_name>\S+) version (?<app_vers>\S+) type (?<app_type>\S+))$
explanation: The module installed in slot slot_num was running an unsupported application version or type.

explanation: The version of software running on the module in slot slot was not the version required by another module.

regex: 414005: TCP Syslog Server (?<intf>\S+) : (?<ip_address>\S+) /(?<port>\S+) connected, New (?<connections>\d+) are permitted based on logging permit\-hostdown policy$
explanation: The TCP syslog server for remote host logging was successful, is connected to the server, and new connections are permitted based on the logging permit-hostdown policy. If the logging permit-hostdown policy is configured, a new connection is permitted.

regex: 419001: Dropping TCP packet from (?<src_interface>\S+):(?<src_ip>\S+)/(?<src_port>\d+) to (?<dst_interface>\S+):(?<dest_ip>\S+)/(?<dst_port>\d+), reason: (?<reason>\S+), MSS (?<size>\S+), data (?<size_2>\S+)$

A duplicate TCP SYN was received during the three-way-handshake that has a different initial sequence number from the SYN that opened the embryonic connection. This may indicate that SYNs are being spoofed. This message occurs in Release 7.0.4.1 and later.

A TCP connection was closed by Dead Connection Detection (DCD) as it is no longer required.

regex: 420001: IPS card not up and fail\-close mode used, dropping (?<icmp>\S+) packet from (?<ifc_in>\S+):(?<sip>\S+)/(?<port>\S+) to (?<ifc_out>\S+):(?<dip>\S+)/(?<port_2>\S+)$

explanation: Packets are dropped when the IPS fail-close mode is used, and the virtual sensor used for the packet is not present.
A packet was dropped (Error Message 1) or skipped (Error Message 2) because the CSC SSM application failed. By default, this message is rate limited to 1 message every 10 seconds.

regex: ^(?:%ASA-\d+-426004: PORT\-CHANNEL:Interface (?<ifc_name1>\S+) is not compatible with (?<ifc_name>\S+) and will be suspended \((?<speed_of>\S+) (?<ifc_name1_2>\S+) is (?<x_mbps>\S+), (?<y>\S+) is (?<g_1000_mbps>\S+)\)|%ASA-\d+-426004: Interface (?<ifc_name1>\S+) is not compatible with (?<ifc_name1_2>\S+) and will be suspended \((?<ifc_name1_3>\S+) is (?<full_duplex>\S+), (?<ifc_name1_4>\S+) is (?<half_duplex>\S+)\))$
explanation: The channel-group num mode mode command is executed on a physical interface and there is a speed or duplex mismatch of this physical interface with that of the port channel.

regex: 428002: WAAS confirmed from (?<in_interface>\S+) :(?<ph_1_____ph_2>\S+) to (?<out_interface>\S+) :(?<ph_5_____ph_6>\S+) , inspection services bypassed on this connection\.$
explanation: WAAS optimization was detected on a connection. All layer 7 inspection services, including IPS, are bypassed on WAAS-optimized connections.
Data has been dropped because an SSP is down and a fail-close policy exists.

regex: 431001: RTP conformance: Dropping RTP packet from (?<in_ifc>\S+):(?<src_ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))/(?<src_port>\d+) to (?<out_ifc>\S+):(?<dest_ip>\S+)/(?<dst_port>\d+), Drop reason: (?<drop_reason>\S+) (?<value>\S+)$
explanation: The RTP packet was dropped.

regex: 434001: SFR card not up and fail\-close mode used, dropping (?<protocol>\S+) packet from (?<ingress>\S+):(?<source>\S+)/(?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) to (?<src_port>\d+):(?<egress_interface>\S+)/(?<destination_ip_address>\S+)$
explanation: A packet has been dropped because of a fail-close configuration for the module. Your loss of connectivity for all the flows is caused by redirecting them to the module, because the fail-close configuration is designed to drop all the flows if the module is down.

regex: 444008: (?<license_type>\S+) license has expired, and the system is scheduled to reload in (?<number>\S+) days\. Apply a new activation key to enable (?<license_type_2>\S+) license and prevent the automatic reload\.$

explanation: A shared license client request was unsuccessfully sent or processed by the server.

Agent will transition to the unidentified \(not registered\) state\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-ID_CERT_RENEW_NOT_STARTED: Identity certificate start date not reached yet\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-ID_CERT_RENEW_FAILED: Identity certificate renewal failed\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-ENTITLEMENT_RENEW_FAILED: Entitlement authorization with Cisco licensing cloud failed\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-COMM_FAILED: Communications failure with Cisco licensing cloud\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-CERTIFICATE_VALIDATION: Certificate validation failed by smart agent\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-AUTH_RENEW_FAILED: Authorization renewal with Cisco licensing cloud failed\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-INVALID_TAG: The entitlement tag is invalid\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-INVALID_ROLE_STATE: The current (?<role>\S*) is not allowed to move to the new (?<role_2>\S*)\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-EVAL_WILL_EXPIRE_WARNING: Evaluation period will expire in time\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-EVAL_EXPIRED_WARNING: Evaluation period expired on time\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-ID_CERT_EXPIRED_WARNING: This device's registration will expire in time\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-CONFIG_OUT_OF_SYNC: Trusted Store Enable flag not in sync with System Configuration, TS flag Config flag\.|%ASA-\d+-444303: %SMART_LIC\-3\-REG_EXPIRED_CLOCK_CHANGE: Smart Licensing registration has expired because the system time was changed outside the validity period of the registration period\. The UC-IME license is either on or off. Once enabled, UC-IME can use any number of available TLS sessions, according to the Secure Firewall ASA limit and the K8 export limit.

regex: 447001: ASP DP to CP (?<queue_name>\S+) was full\. Queue length (?<length>\S+), limit (?<limit>\S+)$
explanation: This message indicates a particular data path (DP) to control point (CP) event queue is full, and one or more multiple enqueue actions have failed. If the event contains a packet block, such as for CP application inspection, the packet will be dropped by the DP, and a counter from the show asp drop command will increment. If the event is for punt to CP, a typical counter is the Punt no memory ASP-drop counter.

For a K8 platform, the limit of 250 SRTP crypto sessions is enforced. Each pair of SRTP encrypt or decrypt sessions is counted as one SRTP crypto session. A call is counted toward this limit only when encryption or decryption is required for a medium, which means that if the pass-through is set for the call, even if both legs use SRTP, they are not counted toward this limit.
The licensed host limit was exceeded. This message applies to the ASA 5505 ASA only.

A header length in TCP was incorrect. Some operating systems do not handle TCP resets (RSTs) correctly when responding to a connection request to a disabled socket. If a client tries to connect to an FTP server outside the Secure Firewall ASA and the FTP server is not listening, then it sends an RST. Some operating systems send incorrect TCP header lengths, which causes this problem. UDP uses ICMP port unreachable messages. The TCP header length may indicate that it is larger than the packet length, which results in a negative number of bytes being transferred. A negative number appears by a message as an unsigned number, which makes it appear much larger than it would be normally; for example, it may show 4 GB transferred in one second. This message should occur infrequently.

explanation: The MTU of an SA was changed. When a packet is received for an IPsec tunnel, the corresponding SA is located and the MTU is updated based on the MTU suggested in the ICMP packet. If the suggested MTU is greater than 0 but less than 256, then the new MTU is set to 256. If the suggested MTU is 0, the old MTU is reduced by 256 or it is set to 256—whichever value is greater. If the suggested MTU is greater than 256, then the new MTU is set to the suggested value.

Because the MTU value is already correct, no MTU adjustment is made. This may happen when multiple PMTU messages are received from different intermediate stations, and the MTU is adjusted before the current PMTU message is processed.

regex: 713014: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Unknown Domain of Interpretation \(DOI\): (?<italic_text>.+)$
explanation: The ISAKMP DOI received from the peer is unsupported.

regex: 713016: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Unknown identification type, Phase (?<italic_text>.+), Type (?<id_type>\S+)$
explanation: The ID received from the peer is unknown. The ID can be an unfamiliar valid ID or an invalid or corrupted ID.

regex: 713017: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Identification type not supported, Phase (?<italic_text>.+), Type (?<id_type>\S+)$
explanation: The Phase 1 or Phase 2 ID received from the peer is legal, but not supported.

regex: 713018: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Unknown ID type during find of group name for certs, Type (?<id_type>\S+)$
explanation: Tn internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713024: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Group (?<group>\S+) IP (?<ip>\S+) Received local Proxy Host data in ID Payload: Address (?<ip_2>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received the Phase 2 local proxy ID payload from the remote peer.

regex: 713025: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received remote Proxy Host data in ID Payload: Address (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received the Phase 2 local proxy ID payload from the remote peer.
The Secure Firewall ASA has received the Phase 2 local proxy ID payload of the remote peer, which includes an IP address range.
The Secure Firewall ASA has received the Phase 2 local proxy ID payload of the remote peer, which includes an IP address range.
The local ID payload included the range ID type, and the specified low address was not less than the high address. A configuration problem may exist.
The remote ID payload included the range ID type, and the specified low address was not less than the high address. A configuration problem may exist.

regex: 713034: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received local IP Proxy Subnet data in ID Payload: Address (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Mask (?<netmask>\S+), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
explanation: The local IP proxy subnet data has been received in the Phase 2 ID payload.

regex: 713035: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Group (?<group>\S+) IP (?<ip>\S+) Received remote IP Proxy Subnet data in ID Payload: Address (?<ip_2>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Mask (?<netmask>\S+), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
explanation: The remote IP proxy subnet data has been received in the Phase 2 ID payload.
An internal software error has occurred, and the ISAKMP packet cannot be transmitted.

regex: 713040: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Could not find connection entry and can not encrypt: msgid (?<message_number>\S+)$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred, and a Phase 2 data structure cannot be found.
Secure Firewall ASA is negotiating a tunnel as the initiator.

The IPsec fast path processed a packet that triggered IKE, but the IKE policy lookup failed. This error may be timing related. The ACLs that triggered IKE might have been deleted before IKE processed the initiation request. This problem will most likely correct itself.

regex: 713048: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Error processing payload: Payload ID: id$
explanation: A packet has been received with a payload that cannot be processed.

regex: 713049: Security negotiation complete for (?<tun_type>\S+) type .(?<group_name>\S+). (?<initiator>[^\/]+)\/(?<responder>[^,]+), Inbound SPI ?= ?(?<inbound_spi>\S+), ?Outbound SPI ?= ?(?<outbound_spi>\S+)
explanation: An IPsec tunnel has been started.
An IPsec tunnel has been terminated. Possible termination reasons include:

regex: 713052: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) User \((?<user_2>\S+) \) authenticated\.$
explanation: remote access user was authenticated.

regex: 713056: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Tunnel rejected: SA \((?<sa_name>\S+) \) not found for group \((?<group_name>\S+) \)!$
explanation: The IPsec SA was not found.

regex: 713060: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Tunnel Rejected: User \((?<user_2>\S+) \) not member of group \((?<group_name>\S+) \), group\-lock check failed\.$
explanation: The user is configured for a different group than what was sent in the IPsec negotiation.

The Secure Firewall ASA was not able to find security policy information for the private networks or hosts indicated in the message. These networks or hosts were sent by the initiator and do not match any crypto ACLs at the Secure Firewall ASA. This is most likely a misconfiguration.

regex: 713066: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE Remote Peer configured for SA: (?<sa_name>\S+)$
explanation: The crypto policy settings of the peer have been configured.

regex: 713068: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received non\-routine Notify message: (?<notify_type>\S+) \((?<notify_value>\S+)\)$
explanation: Notification messages that caused this event are not explicitly handled in the notify processing code.

regex: 713072: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Password for (?<user_3>\S+) \((?<user_2>\S+) \) too long, truncating to (?<number>\S+) characters$
explanation: The password of the user is too long.

regex: 713073: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Responder forcing change of (?<italic_text>.+) /(?<italic_text_2>.+) rekeying duration from (?<larger_value>\S+) to (?<smaller_value>\S+) seconds$
explanation: Rekeying durations are always set to the lower of the values proposed by IKE peers. The value of the initiator is the lower one.

regex: 713074: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Responder forcing change of IPsec rekeying duration from (?<larger_value>\S+) to (?<smaller_value>\S+) Kbs$
explanation: Rekeying durations are always set to the lower of the values proposed by IKE peers. The value of the initiator is the lower one.

regex: 713075: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Overriding Initiator's IPsec rekeying duration from (?<larger_value>\S+) to (?<smaller_value>\S+) seconds$
explanation: Rekeying durations are always set to the lower of the values proposed by IKE peers. The value of the responder is the lower one.

regex: 713078: Temp buffer for building mode config attributes exceeded: bufsize (?<available_size>\S+) , used (?<value>\S+)$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred while processing modecfg attributes.

regex: 713112: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Failed to process CONNECTED notify \(SPI (?<spi_value>\S+) \)!$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA was unable to successfully process the notification payload that included the CONNECTED notify type. This may occur if the IKE phase 2 structure cannot be found using the SPI to locate it, or the commit bit had not been set in the received ISAKMP header. The latter case may indicate a nonconforming IKE peer.

regex: 713113: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Deleting IKE SA with associated IPsec connection entries\. IKE peer: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), SA address: (?<internal_sa_address>\S+), tunnel count: (?<count>\S+)$
explanation: An IKE SA is being deleted with a nonzero tunnel count, which means that either the IKE SA tunnel count has lost synchronization with the associated connection entries or the associated connection cookie fields for the entries have lost synchronization with the cookie fields of the IKE SA to which the connection entry points. If this occurs, the IKE SA and its associated data structures will not be freed, so that the entries that may point to it will not have a stale pointer.

regex: 713114: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Connection entry \(conn entry internal address\) points to IKE SA \((?<sa_internal_address>\S+) \) for peer (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), but cookies don't match$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713115: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client rejected NAT enabled IPsec request, falling back to standard IPsec$
explanation: The client rejected an attempt by the Secure Firewall ASA to use IPsec over UDP. IPsec over UDP is used to allow multiple clients to establish simultaneous tunnels to the Secure Firewall ASA through a NAT device. The client may have rejected the request, either because it does not support this feature or because it is configured not to use it.

regex: 713117: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received Invalid SPI notify \(SPI (?<spi_value>\S+) \)!$
explanation: The IPsec SA identified by the SPI value is no longer active on the remote peer, which might indicate that the remote peer has rebooted or been reset.

regex: 713118: Detected invalid Diffie\-Helmann (?<group_descriptor>\S+) (?<group_number>\S+), in IKE area$
explanation: The group_descriptor field included an unsupported value. Currently we support only groups 1, 2, 5, and 7. In the case of a centry, the group_descriptor field may also be set to 0 to indicate that perfect forward secrecy is disabled.

regex: 713119: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Group (?<group>\S+) IP (?<ip>\S+) PHASE 1 COMPLETED$
explanation: IKE Phase 1 has completed successfully.

regex: 713120: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) PHASE 2 COMPLETED \(msgid=(?<msg_id>\S+) \)$
explanation: IKE Phase 2 has completed successfully.

regex: 713123: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE lost contact with remote peer, deleting connection \(keepalive type: (?<keepalive_type>\S+) \)$
explanation: The remote IKE peer did not respond to keepalives within the expected window of time, so the connection to the IKE peer was terminated. The message includes the keepalive mechanism used.

regex: 713124: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received DPD sequence number (?<rcv_sequence>\S+) in (?<italic_text>.+)$
explanation: The remote IKE peer sent a DPD with a sequence number that did not match the expected sequence number. The packet is discarded. This might indicate a packet loss problem with the network.

regex: 713127: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Xauth required but selected Proposal does not support xauth, Check priorities of ike xauth proposals in ike proposal list$
explanation: The peer wanted to perform a XAUTH, but the Secure Firewall ASA did not choose the XAUTH IKE proposal.

regex: 713129: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received unexpected Transaction Exchange payload type: (?<payload_id>\S+)$
explanation: An unexpected payload has been received during XAUTH or Mode Cfg, which may indicate that the two peers are out-of-sync, that the XAUTH or Mode Cfg versions do not match, or that the remote peer is not complying with the appropriate RFCs.

regex: 713130: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received unsupported transaction mode attribute: (?<attribute>.*) id$
explanation: The device received a request for a valid transaction mode attribute (XAUTH or Mode Cfg) that is currently not supported. This is generally a benign condition.

regex: 713131: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received unknown transaction mode attribute: (?<attribute_id>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received a request for a transaction mode attribute (XAUTH or Mode Cfg) that is outside the range of known attributes. The attribute may be valid but only supported in later versions of configuration mode, or the peer may be sending an illegal or proprietary value. This should not cause connectivity problems, but may affect the functionality of the peer.
A request for an IP address for a remote access client from the internal utility that provides these addresses cannot be satisfied.

regex: 713133: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Mismatch: Overriding phase 2 DH Group\(DH group (?<italic_text>.+) \) with phase 1 group\(DH group (?<italic_text_2>.+)$
explanation: The configured Phase 2 PFS Group differed from the DH group that was negotiated for Phase 1.

regex: 713134: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Mismatch: P1 Authentication algorithm in the crypto map entry different from negotiated algorithm for the L2L connection$
explanation: The configured LAN-to-LAN proposal is different from the one accepted for the LAN-to-LAN connection. Depending on which side is the initiator, different proposals will be used.
The tunnel is being redirected because of load balancing on the remote Secure Firewall ASA. A REDIRECT_CONNECTION notify packet was received.

regex: 713136: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE session establishment timed out \[(?<ike_state_name>\S+) \], aborting!$
explanation: The Reaper has detected an Secure Firewall ASA stuck in an inactive state. The Reaper will try to remove the inactive Secure Firewall ASA.

regex: 713137: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Reaper overriding refCnt \[(?<ref_count>\S+)\] and tunnelCnt \[(?<tunnel_count>\S+)\] \-\- deleting SA!$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713139: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<group_name>\S+) not found, using BASE GROUP default preshared key$
explanation: No tunnel group exists in the group database with the same name as the IP address of the peer. In Main Mode, the Secure Firewall ASA will fall back and use the default preshared key configured in the default group.

regex: 713140: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Split Tunneling Policy requires network list but none configured$
explanation: The split tunneling policy is set to either split tunneling or to allow local LAN access. A split tunneling ACL must be defined to represent the information required by the VPN client.

regex: 713141: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client\-reported firewall does not match configured firewall: (?<action>\S+) tunnel\. Received \-\- Vendor: vendor(id), Product product(id), Caps: (?<capability_value>\S+) \. Expected \-\- Vendor: vendor(id), Product: product(id), Caps: (?<capability_value_2>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA installed on the client does not match the configured required Secure Firewall ASA. This message lists the actual and expected values, and whether the tunnel is terminated or allowed.

regex: 713142: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client did not report firewall in use, but there is a configured firewall: (?<action>\S+) tunnel\. Expected \-\- Vendor: vendor(id), Product product(id), Caps: (?<capability_value>\S+)$
explanation: The client did not report an Secure Firewall ASA in use using ModeCfg, but one is required. The event lists the expected values and whether the tunnel is terminated or allowed. Note that the number following the product string is a bitmask of all of the allowed products.

regex: 713143: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Processing firewall record\. Vendor: vendor(id), Product: product(id), Caps: (?<capability_value>\S+), Version Number: (?<version_number>\S+), Version String: (?<version_text>\S+)$
explanation: Debugging information about the Secure Firewall ASA installed on the client appears.

regex: 713145: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Detected Hardware Client in network extension mode, adding static route for address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: A tunnel with a hardware client in network extension mode has been negotiated, and a static route is being added for the private network behind the hardware client. This configuration enables the Secure Firewall ASA to make the remote network known to all the routers on the private side of the headend.

regex: 713146: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Could not add route for Hardware Client in network extension mode, address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred. A tunnel with a hardware client in network extension mode has been negotiated, and an attempt to add the static route for the private network behind the hardware client failed. The routing table may be full, or a possible addressing error has occurred.

regex: 713147: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Terminating tunnel to Hardware Client in network extension mode, deleting static route for address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: A tunnel to a hardware client in network extension mode is being removed, and the static route for the private network is being deleted behind the hardware client.

regex: 713148: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Terminating tunnel to Hardware Client in network extension mode, unable to delete static route for address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: While a tunnel to a hardware client in network extension mode was being removed, a route to the private network behind the hardware client cannot be deleted. This might indicate an addressing or software problem.

regex: 713149: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Hardware client security attribute (?<attribute_name>\S+) was enabled but not requested\.$
explanation: The headend Secure Firewall ASA has the specified hardware client security attribute enabled, but the attribute was not requested by the VPN 3002 hardware client.

regex: 713152: IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Unable to obtain any rules from filter (?<acl_tag>\S+) to send to client for CPP, terminating connection\.$
explanation: The client is required to use CPP to provision its Secure Firewall ASA, but the headend device was unable to obtain any ACLs to send to the client. This is probably due to a misconfiguration.

regex: DNS\s+lookup\s+for\s+(?<peer_description>(?:\S+\s+)*\S+)\s+Server\s*\[\s*(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*\]\s+(?<answer>[^\!\s]+)
explanation: This message appears when a DNS lookup for the specified server has not been resolved.

regex: 713158: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client rejected NAT enabled IPsec Over UDP request, falling back to IPsec Over TCP$
explanation: The client is configured to use IPsec over TCP. The client rejected the attempt by the Secure Firewall ASA to use IPsec over UDP.

regex: Remote\s+user\s*\(\s*session\s*Id\s*-\s*(?<session_id>\S+)\s*\)\s+has\s+been\s+(?<action>\S+)
explanation: Normal authentication of the remote user to the Secure Firewall ASA server has occurred.

regex: 713161: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Remote (?<user_2>\S+) \(session Id \- (?<id>\S+) \) network access has been restricted by the Firewall Server$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA server has sent the Secure Firewall ASA a message indicating that this user must be restricted. There are several reasons for this, including Secure Firewall ASA software upgrades or changes in permissions. The Secure Firewall ASA server will transition the user back into full access mode as soon as the operation has been completed.

regex: 713162: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Remote (?<user_2>\S+) \(session Id \- (?<id>\S+) \) has been rejected by the Firewall Server$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA server has rejected this user.

regex: 713163: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Remote (?<user_2>\S+) \(session Id \- (?<id>\S+) \) has been terminated by the Firewall Server$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA server has terminated this user session, which can occur if the integrity agent stops running on the client machine or if the security policy is modified by the remote user in any way.

regex: 713165: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client IKE Auth mode differs from the group's configured Auth mode$
explanation: The client negotiated with preshared keys while its tunnel group points to a policy that is configured to use digital certificates.

regex: Headend\s*security\s+gateway\s+has\s+(?<vendor_action>\S+).+check\s+configured
explanation: The hardware client has failed extended authentication. This is most likely a username and password problem or an authentication server issue.

regex: Remote\s+peer\s+has\s+(?<vendor_action>\S+)\s+
explanation: The remote user has failed to extend authentication. This is most likely a username or password problem, or an authentication server issue.

regex: 713169: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE Received delete for rekeyed SA IKE peer: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), SA address: (?<internal_sa_address>\S+), tunnelCnt: (?<tunnel_count>\S+)$
explanation: IKE has received a delete message from the remote peer to delete its old IKE SA after a rekey has completed.

regex: 713170: Group (?<group>\S+) IP (?<ip>\S+) IKE Received delete for rekeyed centry IKE peer: (?<ip_2>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) , centry address: (?<internal_address>\S+) , msgid: (?<id>\S+)$
explanation: IKE has received a delete message from the remote peer to delete its old centry after Phase 2 rekeying is completed.

regex: 713171: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) NAT\-Traversal sending NAT\-Original\-Address payload$
explanation: UDP-Encapsulated-Transport was either proposed or selected during Phase 2. Send this payload for NAT-Traversal in this case.

regex: 713172: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Automatic NAT Detection Status: Remote end (?<is>\S+) \|(?<italic_text>.+) behind a NAT device This end (?<is_2>\S+) \|(?<italic_text_2>.+) behind a NAT device$
explanation: NAT-Traversal auto-detected NAT.

regex: 713174: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Hardware Client connection rejected! Network Extension Mode is not allowed for this group!$
explanation: A hardware client is attempting to tunnel in using network extension mode, but network extension mode is not allowed.

regex: 713176: (?<device_type>\S+) memory resources are critical, IKE key acquire message on (?<interface>\S+) (?<interface_number>\S+) , for Peer (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) ignored$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA is processing data intended to trigger an IPsec tunnel to the indicated peer. Because memory resources are at a critical state, it is not initiating any more tunnels. The data packet has been ignored and dropped.

regex: 713177: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received remote Proxy Host FQDN in ID Payload: Host Name: (?<host_name>\S+) Address (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
explanation: A Phase 2 ID payload containing an FQDN has been received from the peer.

regex: 713178: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE Initiator received a packet from its peer without a Responder cookie$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713179: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE AM Initiator received a packet from its peer without a (?<payload_type>\S+) payload$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713182: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE could not recognize the version of the client! IPsec Fragmentation Policy will be ignored for this connection!$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713184: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Client Type: (?<client_type>\S+) Client Application Version: (?<application_version_string>\S+)$
explanation: The client operating system and application version appear. If the information is not available, then N/A will be indicated.

regex: Error\s*:\s*Username\s+too\s+long\s*-\s*connection\s+(?<action>\w+)
explanation: The client returned an invalid length username, and the tunnel was torn down.
The IKE peer that is attempting to bring up this tunnel is not the one that is configured in the ISAKMP configuration that is bound to the received remote subnet.
The IP address from the pool is either the network or broadcast address for this subnet. This address will be marked as unavailable.
The reference counter for this SA is invalid.

regex: 713193: Received packet with missing payload, Expected payload: (?<payload_id>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received an encrypted or unencrypted packet of the specified exchange type that had one or more missing payloads. This usually indicates a problem on the peer.

regex: 713194: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Sending (?<ike>\S+) \|(?<ipsec>\S+) Delete With Reason message: (?<termination_reason>\S+)$
explanation: A delete message with a termination reason code was received.

regex: 713195: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Tunnel rejected: Originate\-Only: Cannot accept incoming tunnel yet!$
explanation: The originate-only peer can accept incoming connections only after it brings up the first P2 tunnel. At that point, data from either direction can initiate additional Phase 2 tunnels.

regex: 713196: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Remote L2L Peer (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) initiated a tunnel with same outer and inner addresses\. Peer could be Originate Only \- Possible misconfiguration!$
explanation: The remote L2L peer has initiated a public-public tunnel. The remote L2L peer expects a response from the peer at the other end, but does not receive one, because of a possible misconfiguration.

regex: 713197: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) The configured Confidence Interval of (?<number>\S+) seconds is invalid for this (?<tunnel_type>\S+) connection\. Enforcing the second default\.$
explanation: The configured confidence interval in the group is outside of the valid range.

regex: User\s+Authorization\s+(?<vendor_action>[^:\s]+)\s*:\s*(?<user>\S+)
explanation: A reason string that states that a username cannot be found in the certificate appears.

regex: 713201: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Duplicate Phase (?<phase>\S+) packet detected\.(?<action>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has received a duplicate of a previous Phase 1 or Phase 2 packet, and will transmit the last message. A network performance or connectivity issue may have occurred, in which the peer is not receiving sent packets in a timely manner.
This message indicates that a route to the peer-assigned address or to the networks protected by a hardware client was added to the routing table.

An attempt to add a route to the client-assigned address or to the networks protected by a hardware client failed. This might indicate duplicate routes in the routing table or a corrupted network address. The duplicate routes might be caused by routes that were not cleaned up correctly or by having multiple clients sharing networks or addresses.

regex: 713206: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Tunnel Rejected: Conflicting protocols specified by tunnel\-group and group\-policy$
explanation: A tunnel was dropped because the allowed tunnel specified in the group policy was different from the allowed tunnel in the tunnel group configuration.

regex: 713207: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Terminating connection: IKE Initiator and tunnel group specifies L2TP Over IPSec$
explanation: This syslog is displayed for ikev1 while terminating the connection if GW is an initiator and tunnel group type is L2TP over IPSEC.

regex: 713211: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Adding static route for L2L peer coming in on a dynamic map\. address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: The ASA is adding a route for the private address or networks of the peer. In this case, the peer is either a client or a L2L peer with an unknown address. Both of these cases use dynamic crypto maps to allow the tunnel.

regex: 713212: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Could not add route for L2L peer coming in on a dynamic map\. address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) , mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA failed while attempting to add a route for the private address or networks of the peer. In this case, the peer is either a client or a L2L peer with an unknown address. Both of these cases use dynamic crypto maps to allow the tunnel. This might indicate duplicate routes, a full routing table, or a failure of the Secure Firewall ASA to remove previously used routes. Check the routing table to make sure there is room for additional routes and that obsolete routes are not present. If the table is full or includes obsolete routes, remove the routes and try again. If the problem persists, contact the Cisco TAC.

regex: 713213: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Deleting static route for L2L peer that came in on a dynamic map\. address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA is deleting a route for the private address or networks of the peer. In this case, the peer is either a client or a L2L peer with an unknown address. Both of these cases use dynamic crypto maps to allow the tunnel.

regex: 713214: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Could not delete route for L2L peer that came in on a dynamic map\. address: (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), mask: (?<netmask>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA experienced a failure while deleting a route for the private address or networks of the peer. In this case, the peer is either a client or a L2L peer with an unknown address. Both of these cases use dynamic crypto maps to allow the tunnel. The route may have already been deleted,or an internal software error has occurred.

regex: 713215: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) No match against Client Type and Version rules\. Client: (?<italic_text>.+) /(?<is>\S+) not allowed by default$
explanation: The client type and the version of a client did not match any of the rules configured on the Secure Firewall ASA. The default action appears.

regex: 713216: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Rule: (?<action>\S+) \[Client type\]: (?<version>\S+) Client: (?<type>\S+) version allowed/not allowed$
explanation: The client type and the version of a client have matched one of the rules. The results of the match and the rule are displayed.

regex: 713217: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Skipping unrecognized rule: action: (?<action>\S+) client type: (?<client_type>\S+) client version: (?<client_version>\S+)$
explanation: A malformed client type and version rule exist. The required format is action client type | client version action. Either permit or deny client type and client version are displayed under Session Management. Only one wildcard per parameter (*) is supported.

regex: 713218: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Tunnel Rejected: Client Type or Version not allowed\.$
713219: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Queuing KEY\-ACQUIRE messages to be processed when P1 SA is complete\.$
explanation: Phase 2 messages are being enqueued after Phase 1 completes.

regex: 713220: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) De\-queuing KEY\-ACQUIRE messages that were left pending\.$
explanation: Queued Phase 2 messages are being processed.

regex: 713221: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Static Crypto Map check, checking map = (?<crypto_map_tag>\S+), seq = (?<ph_4>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA is iterating through the crypto maps looking for configuration information.
While iterating through the configured crypto maps, the Secure Firewall ASA cannot match any of the associated ACLs. This generally means that an ACL was misconfigured.

regex: 713223: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Static Crypto Map check, map = (?<crypto_map_tag>\S+), seq = (?<seq_number>\S+), no ACL configured$
explanation: The crypto map associated with this peer is not linked to an ACL.

regex: 713224: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Static Crypto Map Check by\-passed: Crypto map entry incomplete!$
explanation: The crypto map associated with this VPN tunnel is missing critical information.

regex: 713225: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) \[IKEv1\], Static Crypto Map check, map (?<map_name>\S+), seq = (?<sequence_number>\S+) is a successful match$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA found a valid matching crypto map for this VPN tunnel.

regex: 713226: Connection failed with peer (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), no trust\-point defined in tunnel\-group (?<tunnel_group>\S+)$
explanation: When the device is configured to use digital certificates, a trustpoint must be specified in the configuration. When the trustpoint is missing from the configuration, this message is generated to flag an error.

regex: 713227: IP = (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) Rejecting new IPsec SA negotiation for peer (?<peer_address>\S+) \. A negotiation was already in progress for local Proxy (?<local_address>\S+) /(?<local_netmask>\S+), remote Proxy (?<remote_address>\S+) /(?<remote_netmask>\S+)$
explanation: When establishing a Phase SA, the Secure Firewall ASA will reject a new Phase 2 matching this proxy.

regex: 713229: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Auto Update \- Notification to client (?<client_ip>\S+) of update string: (?<message_string>\S+) \.$
explanation: A VPN remote access client is notified that updated software is available for download. The remote client user is responsible for choosing to update the client access software.

regex: 713230: Internal Error, (?<ike_lock>\S+) trying to lock bit that is already locked for type (?<type>\S+)$
explanation: An internal error occurred, which is reporting that the IKE subsystem is attempting to lock memory that has already been locked. This indicates errors on semaphores that are used to protect memory violations for IKE SAs. This message does not indicate that anything is seriously wrong. However, an unexpected event has occurred, and steps are automatically being taken for recovery.

regex: 713231: Internal Error, (?<ike_lock>\S+) trying to unlock bit that is not locked for type (?<type>\S+)$
explanation: An internal error has occurred, which is reporting that the IKE subsystem is attempting to unlock memory that is not currently locked. This indicates errors on semaphores that are used to protect memory violations for IKE SAs. This message does not indicate that anything is seriously wrong. However, an unexpected event has occurred, and steps are automatically being taken for recovery.

regex: 713232: SA lock refCnt = (?<value>\S+) , bitmask = (?<hexvalue>\S+) , (?<p1_decrypt_cb>\S+) = (?<value_2>\S+) , (?<qm_decrypt_cb>\S+) = (?<value_3>\S+) , (?<qm_hash_cb>\S+) = (?<value_4>\S+) , (?<qm_spi_ok_cb>\S+) = (?<value_5>\S+) , (?<qm_dh_cb>\S+) = (?<value_6>\S+) , (?<qm_secret_key_cb>\S+) = (?<value_7>\S+) , (?<qm_encrypt_cb>\S+) = (?<value_8>\S+)$
explanation: All the IKE SA are locked, and a possible error has been detected. This message reports errors on semaphores that are used to protect memory violations for IKE SAs.

regex: 713235: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Attempt to send an IKE packet from standby unit\. Dropping the packet!$
explanation: Normally, IKE packets should never be sent from the standby unit to the remote peer. If such an attempt is made, an internal logic error may have occurred. The packet never leaves the standby unit because of protective code. This message facilitates debugging.

regex: 713236: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) IKE_DECODE tx/rx Message \(msgid=msgid\) with payloads:payload1 \((?<payload1_len>\S+)\) \+ payload2 \((?<payload2_len>\S+)\)\.\.\.total length: tlen$
explanation: IKE sent or received various messages. The following example shows the output when IKE receives a message with an 8-byte hash payload, an 11-byte notify payload, and two 13-byte vendor-specific payloads:

regex: 713237: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) ACL update \((?<access_list>\S+) \) received during re\-key re\-authentication will not be applied to the tunnel\.$
explanation: The Phase 1 rekey of a remote access IPsec tunnel appears under the following conditions:

regex: 713238: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Invalid source proxy address: 0\.0\.0\.0! Check private address on remote client$
explanation: The private side address of a network extension mode client came across as 0.0.0.0. This usually indicates that no IP address was set on the private interface of the hardware client.

regex: 713239: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<ip_address>\S+) : Tunnel Rejected: The maximum tunnel count allowed has been reached$
explanation: An attempt to create a tunnel has occurred after the maximum number of tunnels allowed has been reached.

regex: 713242: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Remote (?<user_2>\S+) is authenticated using Hybrid Authentication\. Not starting IKE rekey\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has detected a request to start an IKE rekey for a tunnel configured to use Hybrid Xauth, but the rekey was not started. The Secure Firewall ASA will wait for the client to detect and initiate an IKE rekey.

regex: 713244: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Received Legacy Authentication Method\(LAM\) type (?<type>\S+) is different from the last type received (?<type_2>\S+) \.$
explanation: The LAM attribute type received differs from the last type received. The type must be consistent throughout the user authentication process. The user authentication process cannot proceed, and the VPN connection will not be established.

regex: 713245: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Unknown Legacy Authentication Method\(LAM\) type (?<type>\S+) received\.$
explanation: An unsupported LAM type was received during the CRACK challenge or response user authentication process. The user authentication process cannot proceed, and the VPN connection will not be established.

regex: 713246: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Unknown Legacy Authentication Method\(LAM\) attribute type (?<type>\S+) received\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received an unknown LAM attribute type, which should not cause connectivity problems, but might affect the functionality of the peer.

regex: 713247: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Unexpected error: in Next Card Code mode while not doing SDI\.$
explanation: An unexpected error occurred during state processing.

regex: 713248: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Rekey initiation is being disabled during CRACK authentication\.$
explanation: When an IKE SA is negotiated using the CRACK authentication method, the Phase 1 SA rekey timer at the headend expired before a successful rekey. Because the remote client is always the initiator of the exchange when using the CRACK authentication method, the headend will not initiate the rekey. Unless the remote peer initiates a successful rekey before the IKE SA expires, the connection will come down upon IKE SA expiration.

regex: 713249: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Received unsupported authentication results: (?<result>\S+)$
explanation: While negotiating an IKE SA using the CRACK authentication method, the IKE subsystem received a result that is not supported during CRACK authentication from the authentication subsystem. The user authentication fails, and the VPN connection is torn down.

regex: 713250: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Received unknown Internal Address attribute: (?<attribute>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received a request for an internal address attribute that is not recognizable. The attribute might be valid, but not currently supported, or the peer might be sending an illegal value. This should not cause connectivity problems, but might affect the functionality of the peer.

regex: 713251: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) (?<meta_data>\S+) Received authentication failure message$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received a notification message that indicated an authentication failure while an IKE SA is negotiated using the CRACK authentication method. The connection is torn down.

regex: 713252: Group = (?<group>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<ip>\S+) Group = (?<group_2>\S+), Username = (?<user_2>\S+), IP = (?<ip_2>\S+), Integrity Firewall Server is not available\. VPN Tunnel creation rejected for client\.$
explanation: When the group policy is configured to require the client to authenticate with a Zonelab Integrity Server, the server might need to be connected to the concentrator depending on the failure policy configured. If the fail policy is to reject the client connection, this message is generated when a Zonelab Integrity Server is not connected to the Secure Firewall ASA at the time the client is connecting.

regex: 713253: Group = (?<group>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<ip>\S+) Group = (?<group_2>\S+), Username = (?<user_2>\S+), IP = (?<ip_2>\S+), Integrity Firewall Server is not available\. Entering ALLOW mode\. VPN Tunnel created for client\.$
explanation: When the group policy is configured to require a client to authenticate with a Zonelab Integrity Server, the server might need to be connected to the concentrator, depending on the failure policy configured. If the failure policy is to accept the client connection, and provide unrestricted network access, this message is generated when a Zonelab Integrity Server is not connected to the Secure Firewall ASA at the time the client is connecting.

regex: 713254: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Group = (?<groupname_2>\S+), Username = (?<user_2>\S+), IP = (?<peerip_2>\S+), Invalid IPsec/UDP port = (?<portnum>\S+), valid range is (?<minport>\S+) \- (?<maxport>\S+), except port 4500, which is reserved for IPsec/NAT\-T$
explanation: You cannot use UDP port 4500 for IPsec/UDP connections, because it is reserved for IPsec or NAT-T connections. The CLI does not allow this configuration for local groups. This message should only occur for externally defined groups.

regex: 713255: IP = (?<peer_ip>\S+) IP = (?<peer_ip_2>\S+), Received ISAKMP Aggressive Mode message 1 with unknown tunnel group name (?<group_name>\S+)$
explanation: An unknown tunnel group was specified in ISAKMP Aggressive Mode message 1.

regex: 713256: IP = (?<peer_ip>\S+) , Sending spoofed ISAKMP Aggressive Mode message 2 due to receipt of unknown tunnel group\. Aborting connection\.$
explanation: When the peer specifies an invalid tunnel group, the Secure Firewall ASA will still send message 2 to prevent the peer from gleaning tunnel group information.

regex: 713258: IP = (?<var1>\S+) IP = (?<var1_2>\S+), Attempting to establish a phase2 tunnel on (?<var2>\S+) (?<interface>\S+) but phase1 tunnel is on (?<var3>\S+) (?<interface_2>\S+)\. Tearing down old phase1 tunnel due to a potential routing change\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA tries to establish a Phase 2 tunnel on an interface, and a Phase 1 tunnel already exists on a different interface. The existing Phase 1 tunnel is torn down to allow the establishment of a new tunnel on the new interface.

regex: 713259: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Group = (?<groupname_2>\S+), Username = (?<user_2>\S+), IP = (?<peerip_2>\S+), Session is being torn down\. Reason: (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: The termination reason for the ISAKMP session appears, which occurs when the session is torn down through session management.

regex: 713262: IP = (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) Rejecting new IPSec SA negotiation for peer (?<peer_address>\S+) \. A negotiation was already in progress for local Proxy (?<local_address>\S+) /(?<local_prefix_len>\S+), remote Proxy (?<remote_address>\S+) /(?<remote_prefix_len>\S+)$
explanation: When establishing a Phase SA, the Secure Firewall ASA will reject a new Phase 2 SA matching this proxy.

regex: 713263: Group = (?<groupname>\S+), Username = (?<user>\S+), IP = (?<peerip>\S+) Received local IP Proxy Subnet data in ID Payload: Address (?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)), Mask /(?<prefix_len>\S+), Protocol (?<protocol>\S+), Port (?<port>\S+)$
