regex: 717068: ACME Certificate enrollment succeeded for trustpoint (?<tpname>\S+) with CA (?<ca>\S+)\. Received a new certificate with Subject Name (?<subject>\S+), Issuer Name (?<issuer>\S+), Serial Number (?<serial>\S+) ​\.$
explanation: The ACME certificate enrollment is sucessful for the trustpoint.
The maximum number of load-balancing peers has been exceeded. The new peer is ignored.

regex: 718003: Got unknown peer message \[(?<message_number>\S+)\] from \[(?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))\], local version \[(?<version_number>\S+)\], remote version \[(?<version_number_2>\S+)\]$
explanation: An unrecognized load-balancing message was received from one of the load-balancing peers. This may indicate a version mismatch between peers, but is most likely caused by an internal software error.
An internal software error occurred during packet transmission on the load-balancing socket. This mght indicate a network problem.
The Secure Firewall ASA processed a peer timeout.

regex: 718053: Detected duplicate control node, mastership stolen\[(?<mac_address>\S+)\]$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA detected a duplicate director and a stolen director.
The Secure Firewall ASA deleted the load balancing director from its internal tables.

regex: 718057: Queue send failure from ISR, msg type (?<failure_code>\S+)$
explanation: An internal software error has occurred while attempting to enqueue a message on the VPN load balancing queue from an Interrupt Service Routing.

regex: 718058: State machine return code: (?<action_routine>\S+), (?<return_code>\S+)$
explanation: The return codes of action routines belonging to the load balancing finite state machine are being traced.

regex: 718059: State machine function trace: state=(?<state_name>\S+), event=(?<event_name>\S+), func=(?<action_routine>\S+)\.$
explanation: The events and states of the load balancing finite state machine are being traced.

regex: 718065: Cannot continue to run \(public=(?<up>\S+), private=(?<down>\S+), enable=(?<up_2>\S+), control node=(?<down_2>\S+), session=(?<lb_state>\S+)\)\.$
explanation: The load balancing process can not run because all prerequisite conditions have not been met. The prerequisite conditions are two active interfaces and load balancing enabled.
Load balancing requires a secondary address to be added to the outside interface. A failure occurred in adding that secondary address.
The deletion of the secondary address failed, which might indicate an addressing problem or an internal software error.
The cluster IP address is not on the same network as the outside interface of the Secure Firewall ASA.

regex: 718086: Fail to install LB NP rules: type (?<rule_type>\S+), dst (?<interface_name>\S+), port (?<port>\S+)\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA experienced a failure when attempting to create a SoftNP ACL rule to be used in securing the communication between load balancing peers. This may indicate an internal software problem.

regex: 718087: Fail to delete LB NP rules: type (?<rule_type>\S+), rule (?<rule_id>\S+)\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA experienced a failure when attempting to delete the SoftNP ACL rule used in securing the communication between load balancing peers.

regex: 719015: Parsed emailproxy session pointer from (?<src_ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)) (?<user>\S+): mailuser = (?<mail_user>\S+) , vpnuser = (?<vpn_user>\S+) , mailserver = (?<server>\S+)$
explanation: The username string is received from the client in the format vpnuser (name delimiter) mailuser (server delimiter) mailserver (for example: xxx:yyy@cisco.com). The name delimiter is optional. When the delimiter is not there, the VPN username and mail username are the same. The server delimiter is optional. When it is not present, the default configured mail server will be used.

The password string is received from the client in the format, vpnpass (name delimiter) mailpass (for example: xxx:yyy). The name delimiter is optional. When it is not present, the VPN password and mail password are the same.

regex: 720014: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) Phase 2 connection entry \((?<msg_id>\S+)=(?<message_number>\S+) , my cookie=(?<mine>\S+) , his cookie=(?<his>\S+) \) contains no SA list\.$
explanation: No security association is linked to the Phase 2 connection entry.

regex: 720015: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) Cannot found Phase 1 SA for Phase 2 connection entry \((?<msg_id>\S+)=(?<message_number>\S+) ,my cookie=(?<mine>\S+) , his cookie=(?<his>\S+) \)\.$
explanation: The corresponding Phase 1 security association for the given Phase 2 connection entry cannot be found.

regex: 720032: \(VPN\-unit\) HA status callback: id=(?<id>\S+) , seq=(?<sequence>\S+) , grp=(?<group>\S+) , event=(?<event>\S+) , op=(?<operand>\S+) , my=(?<my_state>\S+) , peer=(?<peer_state>\S+) \.$
explanation: The VPN failover subsystem indicated that a status update was notified by the underlying failover subsystem.

regex: 720037: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) HA progression callback: id=(?<id>\S+) ,seq=(?<sequence_number>\S+) ,grp=(?<group>\S+) ,event=(?<event>\S+) ,op=(?<operand>\S+) , my=(?<my_state>\S+) ,peer=(?<peer_state>\S+) \.$
explanation: The status of the current failover progression is reported.

regex: 720048: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) FSM action trace begin: state=(?<state>\S+) , last event=(?<event>\S+) , func=(?<function>\S+) \.$
explanation: A VPN failover subsystem finite state machine function has started.

regex: 720049: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) FSM action trace end: state=(?<state>\S+) , last event=(?<event>\S+) , return=(?<return>\S+) , func=(?<function>\S+) \.$
explanation: A VPN failover subsystem finite state machine function has finished.

An error occurred when the VPN failover subsystem tried to load a cTCP IKE rule on the standby unit during bulk synchronization. The standby unit may be under heavy load, and the new IKE rule request may time out before completion.

A cTCP record is replicated to the standby unit and cannot be updated. The corresponding IPsec over cTCP tunnel may not be functioning after failover. The cTCP database may be full, or a record with the same peer IP address and port number exists already.

An error occurred while the VPN failover subsystem attempted to update an existing cTCP record during bulk synchronization. The cTCP record may have been deleted from the cTCP database on the standby unit and cannot be found.

regex: 720065: \(VPN\-(?<unit>\S+) \) Failed to add new cTCP IKE rule, peer=(?<peer>\S+) , port=(?<port>\S+) \.$
explanation: An error occurred when the VPN failover subsystem tried to add a new IKE rule for the cTCP database entry on the standby unit. The Secure Firewall ASA may be under heavy load, and the request for adding a cTCP IKE rule timed out and was never completed.

regex: 720072: Timeout waiting for Integrity Firewall Server \[(?<interface>\S+) ,(?<ip>\S+) \] to become available\.$
explanation: The Zonelab Integrity Server cannot reestablish a connection before timeout. In an active/standby failover setup, the SSL connection between a Zonelab Integrity Server and the Secure Firewall ASA needs to be reestablished after a failover.

regex: 721002: (?<device>\S+) HA status change: event (?<event>\S+), my state (?<my_state>\S+), peer state (?<peer>\S+)\.$
explanation: The WebVPN failover subsystem receives status notification from the core HA component periodically. The incoming event, the new state of the local Secure Firewall ASA, and the new state of the failover peer are reported.

regex: 721003: (?<device>\S+) HA progression change: event (?<event>\S+), my state (?<my_state>\S+), peer state (?<peer>\S+)\.$
explanation: The WebVPN failover subsystem transitions from one state to another state based on the event notified by the core HA component. The incoming event, the new state of the local Secure Firewall ASA, and the new state of the failover peer are being reported.
The SVC sent a badly framed datagram, which might be caused by an SVC version incompatibility.
The SVC sent a version unknown to the device, which might be caused by an SVC version incompatibility.

regex: 722029: *Group +(?:<\s*)?(?<group>[^\>]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+User\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<user>[^\>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+IP\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<src_ip>[^\>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+(?<signature>\S+)\s+Session\s+(?<vendor_action>\S+)\s*:\s*Conns\s*:\s*(?<total_connections>\d+)\s*,\s*DPD\s+Conns\s*:\s*(?<number_of_reconnections>\d+)\s*,\s*Comp\s+resets\s*:\s*(?<compression_resets>\d+)\s*,\s*Dcmp\s+resets\s*:\s*(?<decompression_resets>\d+)\.?
explanation: The number of connections, reconnections, and resets that have occurred are reported. If connections is greater than 1 or the number of DPD_conns, compression_resets, or decompression_resets is greater than 0, it may indicate network reliability problems, which may be beyond the control of the Secure Firewall ASA administrator. If there are many connections or DPD connections, the user may be having problems connecting and may experience poor performance.

regex: 722030: *Group +(?:<\s*)?(?<group>[^>]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+User\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<user>[^>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s*IP\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<src_ip>[^>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+(?<signature>\S+)\s+Session\s+(?<vendor_action>\S+)\s*:\s*In\s*:\s*(?<inbound_data_bytes>\d+)\s*\(\s*\+(?<inbound_control_bytes>\d+)\s*\)\s*bytes\s*,\s*(?<inbound_data_packets>\d+)\s*\(\s*\+(?<inbound_control_packets>\d+)\s*\)\s*packets\s*,\s*(?<dropped_inbound_packets>\d+)
explanation: End-of-session statistics are being recorded.

regex: 722031: *Group +(?:<\s*)?(?<group>[^>]+)(?:\s*>)?\s*User\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<user>[^>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+IP\s+(?:<\s*)?(?<src_ip>[^>\s]+)(?:\s*>)?\s+(?<signature>\S+)\s+Session\s+(?<vendor_action>\S+)\s*:\s*Out\s*:\s*(?<outbound_data_bytes>\d+)\s+\(\s*\+(?<outbound_control_bytes>\d+)\s*\)\s*bytes\s*,\s*(?<outbound_data_packets>\d+)\s*\(\s*\+(?<outbound_control_packets>\d+)\s*\)\s*packets\s*,\s*(?<dropped_outbound_packets>\d+)
explanation: End-of-session statistics are being recorded. The statistics include data bytes, control packet bytes, data packets, control packets, and dropped packets.

regex: 725002:\s*Device\s+completed\s+SSL\s+handshake\s+with\s+(?<peer_type>\S+)\s+(?<src_interface>.+):(?<src_ip>(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}|[0-9A-Fa-f:]+)\/(?<src_port>\d+)(?:\s+to\s+(?<dest_ip>(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}|[0-9A-Fa-f:]+)\/(?<dest_port>\d+))?(?:\s+for\s+(?<protocol_version>\S+)\s+session\.?)?$
explanation: The SSL handshake has completed successfully with the remote device.
The remote device is trying to resume a previous SSL session.
The SSL handshake with the remote device has failed.
The SSL session has terminated.

regex: 725008:\s*SSL\s+(?<peer_type>\S+)\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+)\s*:\s*(?:(?<src_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<src_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<src_port>\d{1,5})\s+to\s+(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<dest_port>\d{1,5})\s+proposes\s+the\s+following\s+(?<supported_ciphers>\d+)\s+cipher(?:\(s\))?\.?
explanation: The number of ciphers proposed by the remote SSL device are listed.

regex: 725012:\s*Device\s+chooses\s+cipher\s+(?<cipher_name>.+?(?=\s+for))\s+for\s+the\s+SSL\s+session\s+with\s+(?<peer_type>\S+)\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+)\s*:\s*(?:(?<src_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<src_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<src_port>\d{1,5})\s+to\s+(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<dest_port>\d{1,5})
explanation: The cipher that was chosen by the Cisco device for the SSL session is listed.

regex: SSL\s+lib\s+error *\. *Function\s*:\s*(?<function>\S+)\s+Reason\s*:\s*(?<reason>.+?)[\s\.]*$
explanation: The reason for failure of the SSL handshake is indicated.

regex: Device\s+selects\s+trust-point\s+(?<trust_point_name>\S+)\s+for\s+(?<peer_type>\S+)\s+(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+)\s*:\s*(?:(?<src_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<src_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<src_port>\d{1,5})\s+to\s+(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<dest_port>\d{1,5})
explanation: With server-name indication (SNI), the certificate used for a given connection may not be the certificate configured on the interface. There is also no indication of which certificate trustpoint has been selected. This syslog gives an indication of the trustpoint used by the connection (given by interface :src-ip /src-port ).

regex: 725017:\s*No\s+certificates\s+received\s+during\s+the\s+handshake\s+with\s+(?<remote_device>\S+)\s+(?<src_interface>[^\s\:]+)\s*:\s*(?:(?<src_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<src_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<src_port>\d{1,5})\s+to\s+(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*\/\s*(?<dest_port>\d{1,5})\s+for\s+(?<protocol_version>\S+)\s+session
explanation: A remote client has not sent a valid certificate.

regex: 730006: Group (?<groupname>\S+) , User (?<user>\S+) , IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) : is on NACApp AUTH VLAN (?<vlanid>\S+) \.$
explanation: The session is under NACApp posture assessment.

regex: 730008: Group (?<ph_0>\S+) User (?<ph_2>\S+) IP ipaddr, VLAN MAPPING timeout waiting NACApp\.$
explanation: NACApp (Cisco NAC appliance) posture assessment takes longer than the timeout value configured.

regex: 730009: Group (?<groupname>\S+) , User (?<ph_1>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) , CAS (?<casaddr>\S+) , capacity exceeded, terminating connection\.$
explanation: The load capacity of the NACApp (Cisco NAC appliance) CAS is execeeded, the new incoming session that uses it is terminating.

regex: 733100: (?<target>.*) drop rate ?(?<rate_id>.*) exceeded. Current burst rate is (?<burst_rate>\d+) per second, max configured rate is (?<max_burst_rate>\d+); Current average rate is (?<avg_rate>\d+) per second, max configured rate is (?<max_avg_rate>\d+); Cumulative total count is (?<total_count>\d+)
explanation: The specified object in the message has exceeded the specified burst threshold rate or average threshold rate. The object can be a drop activity of a host, TCP/UDP port, IP protocol, or various drops caused by potential attacks. The Secure Firewall ASA may be under attack.

regex: 733101: (?<object_objectip>\S+)\. Current burst rate is (?<rate_val>\S+) per second, max configured rate is (?<rate_val_2>\S+); Current average rate is (?<rate_val_3>\S+) per second, max configured rate is (?<rate_val_4>\S+); Cumulative total count is (?<ph_5>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA detected that a specific host (or several hosts in the same 1024-node subnet) is either scanning the network (attacking), or is being scanned (targeted).

regex: (?:733201: Threat\-detection: Service\[(?<remote_access_client_initiations>\S+)\] Peer\[(?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))\]: failure threshold of (?<threshold_value>\S+) exceeded: adding shun to (?<interface_2>\S+) (?<interface>\S+)\. (?<ikev2_ra_excessive_client_initiation_requests>\S+)|%ASA-\d+-733201: Threat\-detection: Service\[remote\-access\-client\-initiations\] Peer\[(?<peer>\S+)\-(?<ip>\S+)\]: failure threshold of (?<value>\S+) exceeded: adding shun to (?<interface_2>\S+) (?<interface>\S+)\. (?<italic_text>.+)\.)$
explanation: This message appears when the threat-detection service shunned an IP address due to excessive number of remote access client initiation requests to the headend from that host.

regex: 734001:\s*DAP\s*:\s*User\s+(?<user>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*Addr\s*(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*,\s*Connection\s*(?<type>[^:]+)\s*:.+this\s+connection\s*:\s*(?<DAP_record_names>.+)
explanation: The DAP records that were selected for the connection are listed.

regex: 734002: DAP: User (?<user>\S+), Addr (?<ipaddr>\S+): Connection terminated by the following DAP records: (?<string>\S+)$
explanation: The DAP records that terminated the connection are listed.

regex: 734003:\s*DAP\s*:\s*User\s*(?<user>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*Addr\s*(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s*:\s*Session\s*Attribute\s*(?::\s*|\s+)(?<endpoint_attribute_name>[^\/\s]+)\s*(?:\/|=)\s*\"?\s*(?<endpoint_value>(?:\w+\s+)*[\w+\.]+)\s*\"?
explanation: The AAA and endpoint session attributes that are associated with the connection are listed.

regex: 735007: CPU (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), Critical$
explanation: The CPU has reached a critical temperature.

regex: 735008: Chassis Ambient (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), Critical$
explanation: A chassis ambient temperature sensor has reached a critical level.
The CPU temperature is warmer than the normal operating range.

regex: 735016: Chassis Ambient (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), Warm$
explanation: The chassis temperature is warmer than the normal operating range.

regex: 735017: Power Supply (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), OK$
explanation: The power supply temperature has returned to a normal operating temperature.

regex: 735018: Power Supply (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), Critical$
explanation: The power supply has reached a critical operating temperature.

regex: 735019: Power Supply (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), Warm$
explanation: The power supply temperature is warmer than the normal operating range.
The CPU temperature has returned to the normal operating temperature.

regex: 735021: Chassis Ambient (?<var1>\S+): Temp: (?<var2>\S+) (?<var3>\S+), OK$
explanation: The chassis temperature has returned to the normal operating temperature.
The IO hub temperature is warmer than the normal operating range.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*Received\s+message\s+\'?\s*(?<message_type>[^']+)\s*\'?
explanation: The IP address assignment process received a message.

regex: 737002: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Received unknown message '(?<num>\S+)'$
explanation: The IP address assignment process received a message.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*(?:DHCP\s+configured\s*,\s*no\s+viable\s+servers\s+found|Local\s+pool\s+request\s+succeeded)\s+for\s+tunnel-group\s+\'?(?<tunnel_group>(?:\w+\s+)*\w+)\'?
explanation: The DHCP server configuration for the given tunnel group is not valid.

regex: 737004: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), DHCP configured, request failed for tunnel\-group '(?<tunnel_group>\S+)'$
explanation: The DHCP server configuration for the given tunnel group is not valid.

regex: 737005: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), DHCP configured, request succeeded for tunnel\-group '(?<tunnel_group>\S+)'$
explanation: The DHCP server request has succeeded.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*(?:DHCP\s+configured\s*,\s*no\s+viable\s+servers\s+found|Local\s+pool\s+request\s+succeeded)\s+for\s+tunnel-group\s+\'?(?<tunnel_group>(?:\w+\s+)*\w+)\'?
explanation: The local pool request has succeeded.

regex: 737007: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Local pool request failed for tunnel\-group '(?<tunnel_group>\S+)'$
explanation: The local pool request has failed. The pool assigned to the tunnel group may be exhausted.

regex: 737008: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), tunnel\-group '(?<tunnel_group>\S+)' not found$
explanation: The tunnel group was not found when trying to acquire an IP address for configuration. A software defect may cause this message to be generated.

regex: 737009: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), AAA assigned address (?<ip_address>\S+), request failed$
explanation: The remote access client software requested the use of a particular address. The request to the AAA server to use this address failed. The address may be in use.

regex: 737010: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), AAA assigned address (?<ip_address>\S+), succeeded$
explanation: The remote access client software requested the use of a particular address and successfully received this address.

regex: 737011: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), AAA assigned address (?<ip_address>\S+), not permitted, retrying$
explanation: The remote access client software requested the use of a particular address. The vpn-addr-assign aaa command is not configured. An alternatively configured address assignment method will be used.

regex: 737012: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Address assignment failed$
explanation: The remote access client software request of a particular address failed.

regex: 737013: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Error freeing address (?<ip_address>\S+), not found$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA tried to free an address, but it was not on the allocated list because of a recent configuration change.

regex: 737014: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Freeing AAA address (?<ip_address>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA successfully released the IP address assigned through AAA.

regex: 737015: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Freeing DHCP address (?<ip_address>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA successfully released the IP address assigned through DHCP.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*Freeing\s+local\s+pool\s+(?:(?<pool_name>\S+)\s+)?address\s+(?:(?<ip_address>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<host_name>\S+))$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA successfully released the IP address assigned through local pools.

regex: 737017: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), DHCP request attempt (?<num>\S+) succeeded$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA successfully sent a request to a DHCP server.

regex: 737018: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), DHCP request attempt (?<num>\S+) failed$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA failed to send a request to a DHCP server.

regex: 737019: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Unable to get address from group\-policy or tunnel\-group local pools$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA failed to acquire an address from the local pools configured on the group policy or tunnel group. The local pools may be exhausted.

regex: 737023: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Unable to allocate memory to store local pool address (?<ip_address>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA is low on memory.

regex: 737024: IPAA: Session=\\s\*, Client requested address (?<field>\S+), already in use, retrying$
explanation: The client requested an IP address that is already in use. The request will be tried using a new IP address.

regex: 737025: IPAA:Session=(?<session>\S+), Duplicate local pool address found, \(\?:ip-address|(ipv6-address)\) in quarantine$
explanation: The IP address that was to be given to the client is already in use. The IP address has been removed from the pool and will not be reused.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*Client\s+assigned\s+(?:(?<dest_ip>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<dest_host>\S+))\s+from\s+local\s+pool(?:\s+(?<pool_name>\S+))?
explanation: The client has assigned the given address from a local pool.

regex: 737028: IPAA: Session=\\s\*, Unable to send (?<session>\S+) to standby: communication failure$
explanation: The active Secure Firewall ASA was unable to communicate with the standby Secure Firewall ASA. The failover pair may be out-of-sync.

regex: 737029: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Added \(\?:(?<italic_text>.+)\) to standby$
explanation: The standby Secure Firewall ASA accepted the IP address assignment.

regex: ^(?:%ASA-\d+-737030: IPAA: Session=(?<session>\S+), Unable to send \(\?:(?<italic_text>.+)\) to standby: address in use|%ASA-\d+-737030: IPAA:Session=(?<session>\S+), IPv4 address: (?<ip_address>\S+)|%ASA-\d+-737030: IPAA:Session=(?<session>\S+), IPv6 address: (?<ipv6_address>\S+))$
explanation: The standby Secure Firewall ASA has the given address already in use when the active Secure Firewall ASA attempted to acquire it. The failover pair may be out-of-sync.

regex: 737031: IPAA: Session=\\s\*, Removed (?<session>\S+) from standby$
explanation: The standby Secure Firewall ASA cleared the IP address assignment.

regex: 737032: IPAA: Session=\\s\*, Unable to remove (?<session>\S+) from standby: address not found$
explanation: The standby Secure Firewall ASA did not have an IP address in use when the active Secure Firewall ASA attempted to release it. The failover pair may be out-of-sync.
The address assigned by the AAA/DHCP/local pool is already in use.

regex: IPAA\s*:\s*Session\s*=\s*(?<session>[^,\s]+)\s*,\s*\'?\s*(?<message_type>[^']+)\'?
explanation: A message is queued to the IP address assignment. This corresponds with syslog 737001. This message is not rate limited.

This log occurs when the AAA server (internal or external) has specified an address to assign to the user; but this address already in-use. The request is being re-queued without a specified address to fall back to DHCP or local pools.

regex: 737200: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), Allocated (?<ip_address>\S+) from pool$
explanation: This log occurs an address is allocated from a local pool.

regex: 737201: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), Returned (?<ip_address>\S+) to pool \(recycle=(?<recycle>\S+)\)$
explanation: This log occurs when an address returned to a local pool. The recycle flag indicates whether this address should be re-used for the next request. For rare situation, the recycle flag will be FALSE. For example, when there is an address collision , the address has been assigned to a VPN session by other means such as by AAA or DHCP. In this case, we will not immediately try to reuse that address for the next request.

regex: 737202: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), ERROR: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated when an error event is detected related to the VPN FIP database.

regex: 737203: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), WARN: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to warn of an event related to the VPN FIP database.

regex: 737204: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), NOTIFY: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to notify of an event related to the VPN FIP database.

regex: 737205: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), INFO: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to inform of an event related to the VPN FIP database.

regex: 737206: VPNFIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), DEBUG: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to debug an event related to the VPN FIP database.

regex: 737400: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), Allocated (?<ip_address>\S+) from pool$
explanation: This log occurs an address is allocated from a local pool.

regex: 737401: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), Returned (?<ip_address>\S+) to pool \(recycle=(?<recycle>\S+)\)$
explanation: This log occurs an address returned to a local pool. The recycle flag indicates whether this address should be re-used for the next request. For rare situation, the recycle flag will be FALSE. For example, when there is an address collision—the address has been assigned to a VPN session by other means such as by AAA or DHCP. In this case, we will not immediately try to reuse that address for the next request.

regex: 737402: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), Failed to return (?<ip_address>\S+) to pool \(recycle=(?<recycle>\S+)\)\. Reason: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log occurs unable to return an address to an address pool.

regex: 737403: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), ERROR: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated when an error event is detected related to an IP local pool database.

regex: 737404: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), WARN: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to warn of an event related to an IP local pool database.

regex: 737405: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), NOTIFY: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to notify of an event related to an IP local pool database.

regex: 737406: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), INFO: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to inform of an event related to an IP local pool database.

regex: 737407: POOLIP: Pool=(?<pool>\S+), DEBUG: (?<message>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated to debug an event related to an IP local pool database.

regex: 741006: Unable to write Coredump Helper configuration, reason (?<variable_1>\S+)$
explanation: An error occurred when writing to the coredump helper configuration file. This error occurs only if disk0: is full. The configuration file is located in disk0:.coredumpinfo/coredump.cfg.

regex: 742003: failed to save master key for password encryption, reason=(?<reason_text>\S+)$
explanation: An attempt to save the primary key to nonvolatile memory failed. The actual reason is specified by the reason_text parameter. The reason can be an out-of-memory condition, or the nonvolatile store can be inconsistent.

regex: 742004: failed to sync master key for password encryption, reason=(?<reason_text>\S+)$
explanation: An attempt to synchronize the primary key to the peer failed. The actual reason is specified by the reason_text parameter.

regex: 743011: EOBC RPC call failed, return code (?<code>\S+)\.$
explanation: The EOBC RPC client failed to make an RPC to the intended server.

regex: 746006: (?<user>\S+)\-identity: Out of sync with AD Agent, start bulk download$
explanation: The AD agent cannot update the IP-user mapping events on the ASA and the AD agent event log overflows, which causes inconsistency between the AD agent and the ASA IP-user database.

regex: *user-identity\s*:\s*\S+\s+IP-User\s+mapping\s+(?:(?<ip_address>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<host_name>\S+))\s*-\s*(?<domain_name>[^\\\s]+)\s*\\\s*(?<user>\S+)\s+(?<result>\S+)\s*-\s*(?<reason>.+)
explanation: A new user-IP mapping has been added to the user-to-IP address mapping database. The status of the operation (success or failure) is indicated. The success reason is VPN user. The failure reasons include the following: Maximum user limit reached and Duplicated address.

regex: user-identity\s*:\s*\S+\s+IP-User\s+mapping\s+(?:(?<ip_address>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<host_name>\S+))\s*-\s*(?<domain_name>[^\\\s]+)\s*\\\s*(?<user>\S+)\s+(?<result>\S+)\s*-\s*(?<reason>.+)
explanation: A change has been made to the user-to-IP address mapping database. The status of the operation (success or failure) is indicated. The success reasons include the following: Inactive timeout, NetBIOS probing failed, PIP notification, VPN user logout, Cut-through-proxy user logout, and MAC address mismatch. The failure reason is PIP notification.

regex: user-identity\s*:\s*\[\s*FQDN\s*\]\s+(?<fqdn>\S+)\s+\S+\s+(?:(?<ip_address>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<host_name>\S+))
explanation: A fully qualified domain name has become obsolete.

regex: user-identity\s*:\s*\[\s*FQDN\s*\]\s+(?<fqdn>\S+)\s+\S+\s+(?:(?<ip_address>(?:[\d+.]+|[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f]*:[0-9A-Za-f:]*))|(?<host_name>\S+))
explanation: A fully qualified domain name lookup has succeeded.

regex: user-identity\s*:\s*DNS\s+lookup\s+(?:for\s+(?<fqdn>\S+)\s+)?failed\s*,\s*reason\s*:\s*(?<reason>.+)
explanation: A DNS lookup has failed. Failure reasons include timeout, unresolvable, and no memory.

regex: 747001: State machine event queue depleted\. Event \((?<event_id>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex_2>\S+)\) dropped\. Current state (?<state_name>\S+), stack (?<ptr_in_hex_3>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_4>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_5>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_6>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_7>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_8>\S+)$
explanation: The cluster FSM event queue is full, and a new event has been dropped.

regex: 747002: Recovered from state machine dropped event \((?<event_id>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex_2>\S+)\)\. Intended state: (?<state_name>\S+)\. Current state: (?<state_name_2>\S+)$
explanation: The cluster FSM received an event that is incompatible with the current state.

regex: 747003: Recovered from state machine failure to process event \((?<event_id>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex_2>\S+)\) at state (?<state_name>\S+)$
explanation: The cluster FSM failed to process an event for all reasons given.

regex: 747005: State machine notify event (?<event_name>\S+) \((?<event_id>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex>\S+),(?<ptr_in_hex_2>\S+)\)$
explanation: The cluster FSM has notified clients about an event.

regex: 747007: Recovered from founding stray config sync thread, stack (?<ptr_in_hex>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_2>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_3>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_4>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_5>\S+) (?<ptr_in_hex_6>\S+)$
explanation: Astray configuration sync thread has been detected.

regex: 747008: New cluster member "(?<name>\S+)" with serial number (?<serial_number_a>\S+) rejected due to name conflict with existing unit with serial number (?<serial_number_b>\S+)$
explanation: The same unit name has been configured on multiple units.

regex: 747010: Attempted recovery from failed RPC call, message (?<message_name>\S+), return code (?<code_value>\S+)$
explanation: An RPC call failure has occurred. The system tries to recover from the failure.

regex: 747012: Failed to replicate global object id (?<hex_id_value>\S+) in domain (?<domain_name>\S+) to peer (?<unit_name>\S+), continue operation$
explanation: A global object ID replication failure has occurred.

regex: 747013: Failed to remove global object id (?<hex_id_value>\S+) in domain (?<domain_name>\S+) from peer (?<unit_name>\S+), continue operation$
explanation: A global object ID removal failure has occurred.

regex: 747014: Failed to install global object id (?<hex_id_value>\S+) in domain (?<domain_name>\S+), continue operation$
explanation: A global object ID installation failure has occurred.

regex: 747016: Found a split cluster with both (?<unit_name_a>\S+) and (?<unit_name_b>\S+) as control nodes\. Control node (?<role>\S*) retained by (?<unit_name_a_2>\S+), (?<unit_name_b_2>\S+) will leave then join as a data node$
explanation: A split cluster has been found.

regex: 747019: New cluster member (?<name>\S+) rejected due to Cluster Control Link IP subnet mismatch \((?<ip_address>\S+)/(?<ip_mask>\S+) on new unit, (?<ip_address_2>\S+)/(?<ip_mask_2>\S+) on local unit\)$
explanation: The control unit found that a new joining unit has an incompatible cluster interface IP address.

regex: 747021: Control node (?<unit_name>\S+) is quitting due to (?<interface>\S+) health check failure on (?<interface_name>\S+), (?<number_of_times>\S+) times\. Rejoin will be attempted after (?<time>\S+) min\.$
explanation: The control unit has disabled clustering because of an interface health check failure.

regex: 747022: Asking data node (?<unit_name>\S+) to quit because it failed (?<interface>\S+) health check (?<x>\S+) times \(last failure on (?<y>\S+)\), rejoin will be attempted after (?<interface_name>\S+) min\.$
explanation: This syslog message occurs when the maximum number of rejoin attempts has not been exceeded. A data unit has disabled clustering because of an interface health check failure for the specified amount of time. This unit will re-enable itself automatically after the specified amount of time (ms).

regex: 747023: Control node (?<italic_text>.+) is quitting due to Security Service Module health check failure, and control node's Security Service Card state is (?<italic_text_2>.+)\. Rejoin will be attempted after (?<italic_text_3>.+) minutes\.$
explanation: SSM health check failure on data unit; control unit asks data unit to quit with rejoin.

regex: 747024: Asking data node (?<italic_text>.+) to quit due to Security Service Module health check failure, and its Security Service Module state is (?<italic_text_2>.+)\. The data node will decide whether to rejoin based on the configurations\.$
explanation: SSM health check failure on data unit; control unit asks data unit to quit. The data unit would decide whether to rejoin or not.

regex: 747026: New cluster member (?<unit_name>\S+) rejected due to cluster (?<interface>\S+) name mismatch \((?<ifc_name>\S+) on new unit, (?<ifc_name_2>\S+) on local unit\)$
explanation: A control unit found a joining unit that has an incompatible cluster control link interface name.

regex: 747028: Found unit (?<unit_name>\S+)'s (?<interface>\S+)\-mode is (?<mode_name>\S+), different from mine (?<mode_name_2>\S+), ask it to quit\.$
explanation: A control unit found a joining unit that has an incompatible interface-mode, either spanned or individual.

regex: 747037: Asking data node (?<data_node_name>\S+) to quit due to its Security Service Module health check failure (?<num>\S+) times, and its Security Service Module state is (?<state>\S+)\. Rejoin will be attempted after (?<minutes>\S+) minutes\.$
explanation: SSM health check failure on data unit; control unit asks data unit to quit with rejoin.

regex: 747038: Asking data node (?<node_name>\S+) to quit due to its Security Service Module health check failure (?<num>\S+) times, and its Security Service Card state is (?<module>\S+)\. Clustering must be manually enabled on the unit to rejoin\.$
explanation: SSM health check failure on data; control unit asks data unit to quit with rejoin.

regex: 747041: Control node (?<unit_name>\S+) is quitting due to (?<interface_2>\S+) health check failure on (?<italic_text>.+), (?<num_times>\S+) times\. Clustering must be manually enabled on this unit to rejoin\.$
explanation: Interface health check failure on control unit; control unit kicks itself out with rejoin.

regex: 748102: Control node (?<unit_id>\S+) is quitting due to (?<application_name>\S+) Application health check failure, and control node's (?<application>\S+) state is (?<status>\S+)$
explanation: Application health check detects that the control unit is not healthy. The control unit will leave the cluster group.

regex: 748103: Asking data node (?<unit_id>\S+) to quit due to (?<application_name>\S+) Application health check failure, and data node's (?<application>\S+) state is (?<status>\S+)$
explanation: Application health check detects that the data unit is not healthy. Control unit will evict the data node.

regex: 750005: Local: (?<italic_text>.+) Remote: (?<italic_text_2>.+) Username: (?<user>\S+) IPsec rekey collision detected\. I am lowest nonce (?<initiator>\S+), deleting SA with inbound SPI (?<spi>\S+)$
explanation: A rekey collision was detected (both peers trying to initiate a rekey at the same time), and it was resolved by keeping the one initiated by this Secure Firewall ASA because it had the lowest nonce. This action caused the indicated SA referenced by the SPI to be deleted.

regex: 750014: Local:(?<italic_text>.+):(?<italic_text_2>.+) Remote:(?<italic_text_3>.+):(?<italic_text_4>.+) Username:(?<italic_text_5>.+) IKEv2 Session aborted\. Reason: Initial Contact received for Local ID: (?<italic_text_6>.+), Remote ID: (?<italic_text_7>.+) from remote peer:(?<italic_text_8>.+):(?<italic_text_9>.+) to (?<italic_text_10>.+):(?<italic_text_11>.+)$
explanation: For ASA IKEv2, the initial contact (IC) processing is done based on peer IP/Port and ASA IP/Port pairs and the stale sessions get deleted based on these IP/Port pairs. This could be a problem with NAT as IP/Port of peer may change for connections and the stale sessions would not get cleaned up based on IP/Port pairs. As per the IKEv2 RFC , the Initial Contact processing will be switched to use Identity pairs so that the stale sessions can be identified based on peer and ASA identities and clear them. The identities can be IPs, hostnames, Certificate DNs, and so on. This syslog displays the exact reason for clearing the stale sessions. This syslog will be generated on ASA after clearing a stale session from a peer while negotiating a new IKEv2 session with the same peer. This syslog is applicable only for standalone and clustering site-to-site VPNs and not for RA.

regex: 751005: (?<anyconnect>\S+) client reconnect authentication failed\. Session ID: (?<session_id>\S+), Error: (?<error>\S+)$
explanation: A failure occurred during an AnyConnect client reconnection attempt using the session token.

regex: 751008: Group=(?<group>\S+), Tunnel rejected: IKEv2 not enabled in group policy$
explanation: IKE version 2 is not allowed based on the enabled protocols for the indicated group to which a connection attempt was mapped, and the connection was rejected.

regex: 751024: IPv6 User Filter (?<tempipv6>\S+) configured\. This setting has been deprecated, terminating connection$
explanation: The IPv6 VPN filter has been deprecated and if it is configured instead of a unified filter for IPv6 traffic access control, the connection will be terminated.

regex: 751027: Received INVALID_SELECTORS Notification\. Peer received a packet \(SPI= (?<spi>\S+)\)\. The decapsulated inner packet didn't match the negotiated policy in the SA\. Packet destination (?<pkt_daddr>\S+), port (?<pkt_dest_port>\S+), source (?<pkt_saddr>\S+), port (?<pkt_src_port>\S+), protocol (?<pkt_prot>\S+)\.$
explanation: A peer received a packet on an IPsec security association (SA) that did not match the negotiated traffic descriptors for that SA. The peer sent an INVALID_SELECTORS notification containing the SPI and packet data for the offending packet.

regex: 752017: IKEv2 Backup L2L tunnel initiation denied on (?<interface_2>\S+) (?<interface>\S+) matching crypto map (?<name>\S+), sequence number (?<number>\S+) \. Unsupported configuration\.$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA uses IKEv1 to initiate the connection because IKEv2 does not support the backup L2L feature.

regex: 768001: QUOTA: (?<resource>\S+) utilization is high: requested (?<req>\S+), current (?<curr>\S+), warning level (?<level>\S+)$
explanation: A system resource allocation level has reached its warning threshold. In the case of a management session, the resource is simultaneous administrative sessions.

regex: 768002: QUOTA: (?<resource>\S+) quota exceeded: requested (?<req>\S+), current (?<curr>\S+), limit (?<limit>\S+)$
explanation: A request for a system resource would have exceeded its configured limit and was denied. In the case of a management session, the maximum number of simultaneous administrative sessions on the system has been reached.

regex: 768003: QUOTA: (?<management_session>\S+) quota exceeded for (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+): current (?<g_3>\S+),(?<user_3>\S+) limit (?<g_3_2>\S+)$
explanation: The current management session exceeded the configured limits for the user.

regex: 768004: QUOTA: (?<management_session>\S+) quota exceeded for (?<ssh_telnet_http>\S+) protocol: current (?<g_2>\S+), protocol limit (?<g_2_2>\S+)$
explanation: The maximum number of management sessions for the protocol - ssh, telnet, or http exceeded the configured limit.

regex: 769004: UPDATE: (?<asa>\S+) image '(?<src_file>\S+)' failed verification, reason: (?<failure_reason>\S+)$
explanation: The image failed verification from either the copy command or verify command.

regex: 770001: (?<resource>\S+) resource allocation is more than the permitted limit of (?<limit>\S+)\. If this condition persists, the (?<asa>\S+) will be rebooted$
explanation: The CPU or memory resource allocation for the Secure Firewall ASA virtual machine has exceeded the allowed limit for this platform. This condition does not occur unless the setting for the Secure Firewall ASA virtual machine has been changed from that specified in the software downloaded from Cisco.com.

regex: 770002: (?<resource>\S+) resource allocation is more than the permitted limit of (?<limit>\S+), (?<device>\S+) will be rebooted$
explanation: The CPU or memory resource allocation for the Secure Firewall ASA virtual machine has exceeded the allowed limit for this platform. This condition does not occur unless the setting for the Secure Firewall ASA virtual machine has been changed from that specified in the software downloaded from Cisco.com. The Secure Firewall ASA will continue to reboot if the resource allocation is not changed.

regex: 771001: CLOCK: System clock set, source: (?<src>\S+), before: (?<time>\S+), after: (?<time_2>\S+)$
explanation: The system clock was set from a local source.

regex: 771002: CLOCK: System clock set, source: (?<src>\S+), IP: (?<ip>\S+), before: (?<time>\S+), after: (?<time_2>\S+)$
explanation: The system clock was set from a remote source.

regex: 771003: CLOCK: Hardware clock UIP bit is set to 1, for (?<duration>\S+) secs, start time (?<duration_2>\S+) secs, end time (?<duration_3>\S+) secs\. Read clock time from linux system clock$
explanation: Rate-limited.

regex: 772002: PASSWORD: (?<console>\S+) login warning, (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+), cause: password expired$
explanation: A user logged into the system console with an expired password, which is permitted to avoid system lockout.

regex: 772003: PASSWORD: (?<session>\S+) login failed, (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+), IP (?<ip>\S+), cause: password expired$
explanation: A user logged tried to log into the system with an expired password and was denied access.

regex: 772004: PASSWORD: (?<session>\S+) login failed, (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+), IP (?<ip>\S+), cause: password expired$
explanation: A user logged tried to log into the system with an expired password and was denied access.

regex: 774002: POST: error '(?<err>\S+)', func '(?<func>\S+)', engine (?<eng>\S+), algorithm (?<alg>\S+), mode (?<mode>\S+), dir (?<dir>\S+), key len (?<len>\S+)$
explanation: The crypto service provider failed the power on self-test.
A CTS PAC is nearing its expiration date.
A CTS PAC has expired.

regex: 776203: CTS Env: Unable to retrieve data from (?<source_type>\S+): (?<source>\S+), (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: The ASA was unable to retrieve the CTS environment data and SGT name table for one of the following reasons:

regex: 776204: CTS Env: Data from (?<source>\S+) has expired, policies based on security\-group names are enforced using old mappings$
explanation: The CTS environment data and SGT name table have expired, which is likely to occur after unresolved environment data retrieval failures have occurred.

regex: 776301: CTS Policy: Security\-group tag (?<sgt>\S+) is mapped to security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)"$
explanation: The security group tag referenced in the policy is known and the lookup in the security group table is successful. As a result, the tag name mapping is derived.

regex: 776303: CTS Policy: Security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)" is resolved to security\-group tag (?<sgt>\S+)$
explanation: The securitygroup name referenced in the policy was resolved and the lookup in the security group table was successful. As a result, the tag derived from the table is used for policy enforcement.

regex: 776304: CTS Policy: Unresolved security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)" referenced, policies based on this name will be inactive$
explanation: The securitygroup name referenced in the policy cannot be resolved to a tag and the lookup in the security group table failed. AS a result, the policy referencing the name is inactive, but remains in the configuration.

regex: 776307: CTS Policy: Security\-group name for security\-group tag (?<sgt>\S+) renamed from "(?<old_sgname>\S+)" to "(?<new_sgname>\S+)"$
explanation: In the newly downloaded security group table on the ASA, a change in the security group name for a security group tag was detected; however, there was no change in policy status.

regex: 776308: CTS Policy: Previously unknown security\-group tag (?<sgt>\S+) is now mapped to security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)"$
explanation: In the newly downloaded security group table on the ASA, a previously unknown security group tag was found in the table; however, there was no change in policy status.

regex: 776310: CTS Policy: Security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)" remapped from security\-group tag (?<old_sgt>\S+) to (?<new_sgt>\S+)$
explanation: In the newly downloaded security group table on the ASA, a change in the security group tag for a security group name was detected. All policies referencing the name are updated to reflect the new tag, and policies are enforced based on the new tag.

regex: 776311: CTS Policy: Previously unresolved security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)" is now resolved to security\-group tag (?<sgt>\S+)$
explanation: In the newly downloaded security group table on the ASA, a previously unresolved security group name was resolved to a tag, and the new tag can be used to enforce policies.

regex: 776312: CTS Policy: Previously resolved security\-group name "(?<sgname>\S+)" is now unresolved, policies based on this name will be deactivated$
explanation: In the newly downloaded security group table on the ASA, a previously resolved security group name no longer exists. As a result, all policies based on this security group name become inactive, but remain in the configuration.

regex: 776313: CTS Policy: Failure to update policies for security\-group "(?<sgname>\S+)"\->(?<sgt>\S+)$
explanation: An error was encountered in updating the policies. Policy enforcement will continue based on old tag values and is no longer accurate.

regex: 779002: STS: STS and NAT locate different egress (?<interface>\S+) for segment\-id (?<segment_id>\S+), (?<protocol>\S+) from (?<ifc_name>\S+):(?<ip_address>\S+)/(?<port>\S+) to (?<ip_address_2>\S+)/(?<port_2>\S+)\. Packet was discarded$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA tries to create a connection for a VXLAN packet, but the STS lookup table and NAT policy locate a different egress interface.

regex: 801003: Dropping ICMP type=(?<number>\S+), code=(?<code>\S+) from (?<address>\S+) to (?<address_2>\S+) on (?<interface>\S+) (?<interface_name>\S+)$
explanation: Dropping ICMP.

regex: (?:803001: bypass is continuing after power up, no protection will be provided by the system for traffic over (?<interface>\S+)|%ASA-\d+-803001: bypass is continuing after power up, no protection will be provided by the system for traffic over (?<gigabitethernet>\S+) 1/3\-1/4)$
explanation: Informational message to the user that the hardware bypass will be continued after bootup.

regex: 106017: Deny IP due to Land Attack from (?<src_ip>[0-9.]+) to (?<dest_ip>[0-9.]+)
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA received a packet with the IP source address equal to the IP destination, and the destination port equal to the source port. This message indicates a spoofed packet that is designed to attack systems. This attack is referred to as a Land Attack.

regex: 106021: Deny (?<transport>\w+) reverse path check from (?<src_ip>[0-9.]+) to (?<dest_ip>[0-9.]+) on interface (?<interface>.*)
explanation: An attack is in progress. Someone is attempting to spoof an IP address on an inbound connection. Unicast RPF, also known as reverse route lookup, detected a packet that does not have a source address represented by a route and assumes that it is part of an attack on your Secure Firewall ASA. This message appears when you have enabled Unicast RPF with the ip verify reverse-path command. This feature works on packets input to an interface; if it is configured on the outside, then the Secure Firewall ASA checks packets arriving from the outside. The Secure Firewall ASA looks up a route based on the source_address. If an entry is not found and a route is not defined, then this message appears and the connection is dropped. If there is a route, the Secure Firewall ASA checks which interface it corresponds to. If the packet arrived on another interface, it is either a spoof or there is an asymmetric routing environment that has more than one path to a destination. The Secure Firewall ASA does not support asymmetric routing. If the Secure Firewall ASA is configured on an internal interface, it checks static route command statements or RIP, and if the source_address is not found, then an internal user is spoofing their address.

regex: 106022: Deny (?<transport>\w+) connection spoof from (?<src_ip>[0-9.]+) to (?<dest_ip>[0-9.]+) on interface (?<interface>.*)
explanation: A packet matching a connection arrived on a different interface from the interface on which the connection began. In addition, the ip verify reverse-path command is not configured. For example, if a user starts a connection on the inside interface, but the Secure Firewall ASA detects the same connection arriving on a perimeter interface, the Secure Firewall ASA has more than one path to a destination. This is known as asymmetric routing and is not supported on the Secure Firewall ASA . An attacker also might be attempting to append packets from one connection to another as a way to break into the Secure Firewall ASA . In either case, the Secure Firewall ASA shows this message and drops the connection.

regex: 109034: Authentication failed for network (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+) from (?<src_ip>\S+)/(?<port>\S+) to (?<dst_ip>\S+)/(?<port_2>\S+)\. Interactive challenge processing is not supported for (?<protocol>\S+) (?<connections>\d+)$
explanation: AAA challenge processing was triggered during authentication of a network connection, but the Secure Firewall ASA cannot initiate interactive challenge processing with the client application. When this occurs, the authentication attempt will be rejected and the connection denied.

regex: 109035: Exceeded maximum number \(999\) of DAP attribute instances for (?<user_2>\S+) = (?<user>\S+)$
explanation: This log is generated when the number of DAP attributes received from the RADIUS server exceeds the maximum number allowed when authenticating a connection for the specified user.

regex: 109036: Exceeded (?<g_1000>\S+) attribute values for the (?<attribute_name>\S+) attribute for (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+)$
explanation: The LDAP response message contains an attribute that has more than 1000 values.

regex: 109037: Exceeded (?<g_5000>\S+) attribute values for the (?<attribute_name>\S+) attribute for (?<user_2>\S+) (?<user>\S+)$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA supports multiple values of the same attribute received from a AAA server. If the AAA server sends a response containing more than 5000 values for the same attribute, then the Secure Firewall ASA treats this response message as being malformed and rejects the authentication. This condition has only been seen in lab environments using specialized test tools. It is unlikely that the condition would occur in a real-world production network.

regex: 109039: AAA Authentication: Dropping an unsupported IPv6/IP46/IP64 packet from (?<lifc>\S+):(?<laddr>\S+) to (?<fifc>\S+):(?<faddr>\S+)$
explanation: A packet containing IPv6 addresses or IPv4 addresses translated to IPv6 addresses by NAT requires AAA authentication or authorization. AAA authentication and authorization do not support IPv6 addresses. The packet is dropped.

regex: 109040: User at (?<ip>\S+) exceeded auth proxy rate limit of 10 (?<connections>\d+)/sec$
explanation: A connection attempt has been rejected because the ASA has detected a high frequency of HTTPS authentication requests from the same host.

regex: 109105: Failed to determine the egress (?<interface>\S+) for locally generated traffic destined to (?<protocol>\S+) (?<ip>\S+):(?<port>\S+)\.$
explanation: It is necessary for Secure Firewall ASA to log a syslog if no routes are present when the interface is BVI. Apparently, if default route is present and it does not route packet to the correct interface then it becomes impossible to track it.

regex: 110002:\s*Failed\s+to\s+locate\s+egress\s+interface\s+for\s+(?<transport>\S+)\s+from\s+(?:(?<src_interface>[^:\s]+):)?(?<src_ip>\S+)\/(?<src_port>\d+)\s+to\s+(?:(?<dest_interface>[^:\s]+):)?(?<dest_ip>\S+)\/(?<dest_port>\d+)
explanation: An error occurred when the Secure Firewall ASA tried to find the interface through which to send the packet.

regex: 110003: Routing failed to locate next hop for (?<protocol>\S+) from (?<src_interface>\S+):(?<src_ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))/(?<src_port>\d+) to (?<dst_interface>\S+):(?<dest_ip>\S+)/(?<dst_port>\d+)$
explanation: An error occurred when the Secure Firewall ASA tried to find the next hop on an interface routing table.
A flow changed on the egress interface.

regex: 110005: Routing failed to locate next hop for protocol from (?<interface>\S+):(?<address>\S+)/(?<port>\S+) to (?<interface_2>\S+):(?<address_2>\S+)/(?<port_2>\S+)$
explanation: A flow not found during output route lookup.

You have exited the configuration mode. The IP_address value indicates whether the login was made at the console port or through a Telnet connection.

regex: 111007: Begin configuration: (?<source>\S+)
explanation: You have entered the reload or configure command to read in a configuration. The device text can be floppy, memory, net, standby, or terminal. The IP_address value indicates whether the login was made at the console port or through a Telnet connection.

regex: 111008: User (?<user>\S+) executed the '(?<command>[^']+)
explanation: The user entered any command, with the exception of a show command.

regex: 111009:\s*User (?<user>\S+) executed cmd:(?<command>.*)
explanation: The user entered a command that does not modify the configuration. This message appears only for show commands.

regex: 111111: (?<error_message>.+)$
explanation: A system or infrastructure error has occurred.

regex: 113001: Unable to open AAA session\. Session limit \[(?<limit>\S+)\] reached$
explanation: The AAA operation on an IPsec tunnel or WebVPN connection cannot be performed because of the unavailability of AAA resources. The limit value indicates the maximum number of concurrent AAA transactions.

regex: 113003:\s*AAA\s+group\s+policy\s+for\s+user\s+(?<user>\S+)\s+is\s+being\s+(?<action>\S+)\s+to\s+(?<object>.+?)[\.\s]*$
explanation: The group policy that is associated with the tunnel group is being overridden with a user-specific policy, policy_name . The policy_name is specified using the username command when LOCAL authentication is configured or is returned in the RADIUS CLASS attribute when RADIUS authentication is configured.

regex: 113005:\s*AAA\s+user\s+authentication\s+(?<action>\S+)\s*:\s*reason\s=\s(?<reason>.*?)\s:\sserver\s=\s(?<dest_ip>\S+)\s*:\s*user\s=\s(?<user>\S*)(?:\s:\suser\sIP\s=\s*(?<src_ip>\S+))?
explanation: The AAA authentication on a connection has failed. The username is hidden when invalid or unknown, but appears when valid or the no logging hide username command has been configured.

regex: 113006: User '(?<user>\S+)' locked out on exceeding '(?<number>\S+)' successive failed authentication attempts$
explanation: A locally configured user is being locked out. This happens when a configured number of consecutive authentication failures have occurred for this user and indicates that all future authentication attempts by this user will be rejected until an administrator unlocks the user using the clear aaa local user lockout command. The user is the user that is now locked, and the number is the consecutive failure threshold configured using the aaa local authentication attempts max-fail command.

regex: 113007: User '(?<user>\S+)' unlocked by '(?<administrator>\S+)'$
explanation: A locally configured user that was locked out after exceeding the maximum number of consecutive authentication failures set by using the aaa local authentication attempts max-fail command has been unlocked by the indicated administrator.

regex: 113008:\s*AAA.*user = (?<user>\S+)
explanation: The AAA transaction for a user associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection was completed successfully. The user is the username associated with the connection.

regex: 113009:\s*AAA.*group policy (?<group_policy>.*) for user = (?<user>\S+)
explanation: The authentication or authorization of an IPsec or WebVPN connection has occurred. The attributes of the group policy that were specified with the tunnel-group or webvpn commands have been retrieved.
The authentication of an IPsec connection has occurred with a SecurID server. The user will be prompted to provide further information before being authenticated.

regex: 113011:\s*AAA.*group policy (?<group_policy>.*) for user = (?<user>\S+)
explanation: The authentication or authorization of an IPsec or WebVPN connection has occurred. The attributes of the group policy that was specified with the tunnel-group or webvpn commands have been retrieved.

regex: 113012:\s*AAA\s+user\s+authentication\s+(?<action>\S+)\s*:\s*(?<source>.+?)\s*:\s*user\s*=\s*(?<user>\S+)
explanation: The user associated with a IPsec or WebVPN connection has been successfully authenticated to the local user database.

regex: 113013: AAA unable to complete the request Error : reason = (?<reason>\S+) : (?<user_2>\S+) = (?<user>\S+)$
explanation: The AAA transaction for a user associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection has failed because of an error or has been rejected because of a policy violation.

The device was unable to communicate with the configured AAA server during the AAA transaction associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection. This may or may not result in a failure of the user connection attempt depending on the backup servers configured in the aaa-server group and the availability of those servers. The username is hidden when invalid or unknown, but appears when valid or the no logging hide username command has been configured.

regex: 113015: AAA (?<user_2>\S+) authentication Rejected : reason = (?<reason>\S+) : local database : (?<user_3>\S+) = (?<ph_1>\S+) : (?<user_4>\S+) IP = (?<xxx_xxx_xxx_xxx>\S+)$
explanation: A request for authentication to the local user database for a user associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection has been rejected. The username is hidden when invalid or unknown, but appears when valid or the no logging hide username command has been configured.

The AAA transaction for a user associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection has failed because of an error or rejected due to a policy violation. The username is hidden when invalid or unknown, but appears when valid or the no logging hide username command has been configured.

regex: 113017: AAA credentials rejected : reason = (?<reason>\S+) : local database : (?<user_2>\S+) = (?<ph_1>\S+) : (?<user_3>\S+) IP = (?<xxx_xxx_xxx_xxx>\S+)$
explanation: The AAA transaction for a user associated with an IPsec or WebVPN connection has failed because of an error or rejected because of a policy violation. This event only appears when the AAA transaction is with the local user database rather than with an external AAA server.

Authentication for an IPsec or WebVPN user through a Kerberos server has failed because the clocks on the Secure Firewall ASA and the server are more than five minutes (300 seconds) apart. When this occurs, the connection attempt is rejected.

regex: 113021: Attempted console login failed (?<user_2>\S+) '(?<user>\S+)' did NOT have appropriate Admin Rights\.$
explanation: A user has tried to access the management console and was denied.

regex: 113022: AAA Marking (?<protocol>\S+) server \(\?:(?<italic_text>.+)\) in aaa\-server group (?<tag>\S+) as FAILED$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has tried an authentication, authorization, or accounting request to the AAA server and did not receive a response within the configured timeout window. The AAA server will be marked as failed and has been removed from service.

regex: 113023: AAA Marking (?<protocol>\S+) server (?<ip_addr>\S+) in aaa\-server group (?<tag>\S+) as ACTIVE$
explanation: The Secure Firewall ASA has reactivated the AAA server that was previously marked as failed. The AAA server is now available to service AAA requests.

regex: 113025: Group (?<tg>\S+): (?<fields>\S+) Could not authenticate (?<connection_type>\S+) connection from (?<ip>\S+)$
explanation: A username cannot be successfully extracted from the certificate.

regex: 113026: Error (?<error>\S+) while executing Lua script for group (?<tunnel_group>\S+)$
explanation: An error occurred while extracting a username from the client certificate for use in AAA. This message is only generated when the username-from-certificate use-script option is enabled.

regex: 113028: Extraction of (?<user>\S+) from VPN client certificate has (?<string>\S+)\. \[Request (?<num>\S+)\]$
explanation: The processing request of a username from a certificate is running or has finished.

regex: 113029: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) Session could not be established: session limit of (?<num>\S+) reached\.$
explanation: The user session cannot be established because the current number of sessions exceeds the maximum session load.

regex: 113031: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) (?<anyconnect>\S+) 'vpn\-filter (?<filter>\S+)' is an IPv6 ACL; ACL not applied\.$
explanation: The type of ACL to be applied is incorrect. An IPv6 ACL has been configured as an IPv4 ACL through the vpn-filter command.

regex: 113032: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) (?<anyconnect>\S+) 'ipv6\-vpn\-filter (?<filter>\S+)' is an IPv4 ACL; ACL not applied\.$
explanation: The type of ACL to be applied is incorrect. An IPv4 ACL has been configured as an IPv6 ACL through the ipv6-vpn-filter command.

regex: 113033: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) (?<anyconnect>\S+) session not allowed\. ACL parse error\.$
explanation: The WebVPN session for the specified user in this group is not allowed because the associated ACL did not parse. The user will not be allowed to log in via WebVPN until this error has been corrected.

regex: 113035: Group <(?<group>\S+)> User <(?<user>\S+)> IP <(?<ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))> Session terminated: (?<anyconnect>\S+) not enabled or invalid (?<anyconnect_2>\S+) image on the (?<device_name>\S+)$
explanation: The user logged in via the AnyConnect client. The SVC service is not enabled globally, or the SVC image is invalid or corrupted. The session connection has been terminated.

regex: 113036: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) AAA parameter (?<name>\S+) value invalid\.$
explanation: The given parameter has a bad value. The value is not shown because it might be very long.

regex: 113038: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) Unable to create (?<anyconnect_parent>\S+) session\.$
explanation: The AnyConnect session was not created for the user in the specified group because of resource issues. For example, the user may have reached the maximum login limit.

regex: 113040: Group (?<group>\S+) User (?<user>\S+) IP (?<ipaddr>\S+) Terminating the VPN connection attempt from (?<attempted_group>\S+)\. Reason: This connection is group locked to (?<ph_4>\S+)\.$

regex: 113042: Non\-HTTP connection from (?<src_if>\S+):(?<src_ip>(?:\[[^\]]+\]|(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)|[0-9a-fA-F:.]+))/(?<src_port>\d+) to (?<dest_if>\S+):(?<dest_ip>\S+)/(?<dst_port>\d+) denied by redirect filter; only HTTP (?<connections>\d+) are supported for redirection\.$

regex: 114001: Failed to initialize (?<card_type>\S+) I/O card due to (?<error_string>.+?)\.$

explanation: The Smart Call-Home module retrieved an event from the queue to process.

regex: 120004: Call\-Home (?<group>\S+) event (?<title>\S+) was dropped\. Reason: (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: A Smart Call-Home event was dropped. The event may have been dropped because of an internal error, the event queue is full, or the Smart Call-Home module was disabled after the message was generated, but before it was processed.

regex: 120005: Call\-Home (?<group>\S+) message to (?<destination>\S+) was dropped\. Reason: (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: A Smart Call-Home message was dropped. The message may have been dropped because of an internal error, a network error, or the Smart Call-Home module was disabled after the message was generated, but before it was delivered.

regex: 120006: Call\-Home (?<group>\S+) message to (?<destination>\S+) failed\. Reason: (?<reason>\S+)$
explanation: An error occurred while the Smart Call Home module tried to deliver a message. The error may be transient. The message is not dropped when message 120006 is generated. The message may be queued for retransmission. The message is only dropped when message 120005 is generated.

regex: 120007: Call\-Home (?<group>\S+) message to (?<destination>\S+) delivered\.$

regex: 120008: Call\-Home client (?<client>\S+) was activated\.$

regex: 120009: Call\-Home client (?<client>\S+) was deactivated\.$
explanation: The Smart Call Home module is disabled, an event group is enabled, or an event group is no longer subscribed to by any active profile. If these conditions are met, clients of that event group will be deactivated.

regex: 120010: Call\-Home (?<command>\S+) command to client (?<client>\S+) failed\. Reason: (?<reason>\S+)\.$
explanation: The Smart Call Home module notified Smart Call Home clients of certain events through the callback function. If the client does not interpret the command correctly, does not understand the command, or cannot process the command, an error will be returned.

explanation: A software error has occurred. IDB subblocks cannot be removed.

The dynamic DNS subsystem failed to update the resource records on the DNS server. This failure might occur if the Secure Firewall ASA is unable to contact the DNS server or the DNS service is not running on the destination system.
A dynamic DNS update succeeded in the DNS server.
A service from the web cache of the Secure Firewall ASA was acquired.
A service from the web cache of the Secure Firewall ASA was lost.

regex: 334001: EAPoUDP association initiated \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An EAPoUDP association has been initiated with a remote host.

regex: 334002: EAPoUDP association successfully established \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An EAPoUDP association has been successfully established with the host.

regex: 334003: EAPoUDP association failed to establish \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An EAPoUDP association has failed to establish with the host.

regex: 334004: Authentication request for NAC Clientless host \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An authentication request was made for a NAC clientless host.

regex: 334005: Host put into NAC Hold state \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: The NAC session for the host was put into the Hold state.

regex: 334006: EAPoUDP failed to get a response from host \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An EAPoUDP response was not received from the host.

regex: 334007: EAPoUDP association terminated \- (?<host_address>\S+)\.$
explanation: An EAPoUDP association has terminated with the host.

regex: 334009: Audit request for NAC Clientless host \- (?<assigned_ip>\S+)\.$
